items.headline: Ipespe poll: Flávio 48, Lula 46; first runoff debate on Sunday
items.lead: A third poll this week shows the runoff within the margin of error, with the gap narrowing.
items.text: A third poll this week shows the runoff within the margin of error, with the gap narrowing. Ipespe, commissioned by Abrapel and published on 17 October (1,500 telephone interviews, 13–15 October, margin of error 2.6 points, registered as BR-00223/2026), gives Flávio Bolsonaro 48 percent and Lula 46, against 49 to 44 in its previous round. In valid votes the figures are 51.2 to 48.8, down from 52.7 to 47.3. Each candidate is rejected by 47 percent. Among the 89 percent who say they are certain to vote, Flávio leads 50 to 46. Veja and CNN Brasil report the poll. The two candidates meet in their first runoff debate on TV Band on Sunday, 18 October, at 8 p.m. Brasília time (2 a.m. Monday, Israel time), according to BBC Brasil.

items.headline: Elabe: Philippe, Glucksmann and Mélenchon level at about 15 to 16 percent behind Le Pen
items.lead: An Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, taken online from 14 to 16 October among 1,701 people (1,533 registered voters) and published on 17 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 31 to 33.5 percent in the first round, down 1 to 1.5 points since Elabe's August poll.
items.text: An Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, taken online from 14 to 16 October among 1,701 people (1,533 registered voters) and published on 17 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 31 to 33.5 percent in the first round, down 1 to 1.5 points since Elabe's August poll. Behind her three candidates are almost level: Édouard Philippe at 15.5 to 16.5 percent when he is the only centrist, Raphaël Glucksmann at 15 to 16.5 (up 2.5 to 4 points) and Jean-Luc Mélenchon at 15 to 16 (up 1 to 2). Gabriel Attal is at 9.5 to 10.5, Bruno Retailleau at 6.5 to 9.5 and David Lisnard at 5.5 to 6.5; if both Philippe and Attal run, Philippe falls to 13.5 and Attal to 4.5. Natacha Polony, tested for the first time in one scenario, has 1.5 percent. Elabe says 46 percent of those who name a candidate could still change their minds. In the second round Le Pen beats Philippe 52.5 to 47.5 (unchanged since August), Glucksmann 53.5 to 46.5 (57 to 43 in August) and Mélenchon 69 to 31. The margin of error is 1.2 to 2.8 points. The fieldwork ended the day before the violence of 17 October, so the poll does not measure its effect. On Polymarket (about $152 million traded) Le Pen was at about 47 percent on the morning of 18 October, Philippe 17.5, Lisnard 11.5, Mélenchon 10.5 and Glucksmann about 4; this is no material change.

items.headline: 17 October final count: 550,000 marchers by police count, 1,200 arrests, 150 police injured, Limoges town hall burned
items.lead: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 550,000 people marched in about 110 cities on 17 October, 110,000 of them in Paris; the organizers claimed 800,000.
items.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 550,000 people marched in about 110 cities on 17 October, 110,000 of them in Paris; the organizers claimed 800,000. Late on Saturday evening Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu gave a provisional total of 1,200 arrests across France (Nuñez had given about 400 at 8 p.m.) and 150 police officers and gendarmes injured; he said it was "a miracle" the toll was not heavier. Europe 1 reported that one Paris officer is in critical condition with internal bleeding after a projectile hit him on the head. A BFMTV medical source counted at least five people in critical condition in Paris and other, less serious, injuries in Lyon, Lille, Dijon and Rennes. In Saint-Étienne a 17-year-old lost his right hand to a police grenade; he says he picked it up. The prosecutor, Anne Gaches, opened an inquiry and gave it to the police inspectorate (IGPN). In Limoges masked men burned a police car and then set fire to the town hall, which is 143 years old; its roof and bell tower collapsed, and the prefect, Maurice Barate, called the building "largely lost" and "a catastrophe for heritage." Shops were looted in central Paris (around République, the 11th arrondissement, Les Halles and La Madeleine, where a motorcycle dealership was set on fire) and in Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Nice, Marseille, Rennes and other cities. The heads of Carrefour and Intermarché condemned the looting. The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon asked Lecornu to receive them early this week. The figures for arrests and injuries are provisional, and the injury counts come from single outlets.

items.headline: Lecornu tells LFI to "choose its side"; Le Pen blames the far left; Mélenchon blames the government
items.lead: After the violence of 17 October Lecornu told La France insoumise that it was "time to choose your side," the Republic and the police or "the rioters," and spoke of a "point of no return."
items.text: After the violence of 17 October Lecornu told La France insoumise that it was "time to choose your side," the Republic and the police or "the rioters," and spoke of a "point of no return." On X he called attempts to blame police commanders "a dangerous and cynical inversion" and told LFI, "It is YOUR political responsibility." President Macron said those who looted shops, prefectures and town halls "will be prosecuted and punished" and that "we will all stand together against the sowers of chaos." Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin asked for "an extremely firm judicial response." Marine Le Pen said the social demands had been "taken hostage" by the far left and LFI deputies; Jordan Bardella spoke of "professionals of chaos" and Éric Ciotti of "red fascism." Édouard Philippe called for "the greatest firmness"; Bruno Retailleau spoke of violence against police of unprecedented intensity and David Lisnard of a national shame. Jean-Luc Mélenchon said Lecornu had "played with fire, counting on things to rot" and was provoking "a regime crisis"; he called the policing strategy "lamentable" but also said that "those who share our fight have no business in looting." Marine Tondelier (Greens) asked for a review of policing doctrine. Analysis (Florent Barraco, Paris Match): French history since 1968 suggests that disorder usually helps "the party of order," today associated with the National Rally, but the RN has never governed, and far-left promises of street resistance if Le Pen wins make it harder for her to present herself as the guarantee of order. The National Assembly votes on the first part of the 2027 budget on Tuesday, 20 October.

items.headline: Netanyahu: "We're tied"; Bennett and Liberman name their first laws; Eisenkot gives an 18-month Gaza pledge
items.lead: Ten days before the 27 October election, Prime Minister Netanyahu told i24NEWS on 17 October that the race is "tied" and urged his voters to turn out, warning that Iran, Hezbollah and Hamas would try to interfere, including by "creating security incidents."
items.text: Ten days before the 27 October election, Prime Minister Netanyahu told i24NEWS on 17 October that the race is "tied" and urged his voters to turn out, warning that Iran, Hezbollah and Hamas would try to interfere, including by "creating security incidents." Naftali Bennett said a new government would first vote to set up a state commission of inquiry into 7 October, then pass an eight-year term limit for prime ministers and a draft law. Avigdor Liberman wrote that the first steps should be to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana and pass, in three readings, a law barring a defendant from forming a government. Yair Lapid said on Channel 12 that he does not trust Netanyahu on security and that no intelligence justifies preventing the election. Gadi Eisenkot pledged on X that Hamas will not rule Gaza within 18 months of his taking office. No new seat poll was published on Saturday; the Globes average of 17 October gives Likud 22, Yashar 21, Beyachad 12 and the Democrats 9, with the coalition at 54, the opposition parties at 49 and the Arab parties at 13. On Polymarket (about $47.5 million traded) Eisenkot rose to about 54 percent on the morning of 18 October, from about 50 a day earlier; Netanyahu was at about 27.5 and Bennett at 13.5.

items.headline: Lebanon will press for a halt to Israeli strikes at the Tampa talks on 20 October; Qatar pledges a solar plant
items.lead: The Lebanese presidency said on 17 October that its military delegation will demand a halt to Israeli attacks at the US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa on 20 October.
items.text: The Lebanese presidency said on 17 October that its military delegation will demand a halt to Israeli attacks at the US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa on 20 October. The meeting is to cover ceasefire arrangements, the deployment of the Lebanese army in the south and verification. Al-Mayadeen, quoted by Ynet, said the talks would run from 20 to 22 October without political officials and that no date has been set for the eighth round of negotiations. On 16 October Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, visited Beirut and announced a solar power plant to be built by QatarEnergy and TotalEnergies; Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said it would cost the Lebanese state nothing. The Qatari prime minister said Qatar is working with the United States to prepare reconstruction in the south.

items.headline: PoderData ties the runoff at 50–50; Gerp has Flávio 52 to 48; Polymarket back near 80 percent
items.lead: Two more runoff polls were published on 16 October: PoderData/Aya (3,000 telephone interviews, 13–15 October, margin 1.8 points) has Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied at 50 percent of valid votes.
items.text: Two more runoff polls were published on 16 October: PoderData/Aya (3,000 telephone interviews, 13–15 October, margin 1.8 points) has Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied at 50 percent of valid votes. Gerp (2,400 interviews, 14–16 October, margin 2 points) gives Flávio 52 percent of valid votes to Lula's 48, and 50 to 45 in total votes. Poder360's count on 17 October found Flávio numerically ahead in 11 of the 13 latest polls, with Lula ahead only in Vox Brasil; most results are within the margin of error. On Polymarket (about $186 million traded) Flávio rose to about 80 percent on the morning of 18 October, from about 78 a day earlier. The televised runoff debate is on Sunday evening, 18 October (2 a.m. Monday Israel time). The runoff is on 25 October.

items.headline: Amazon blocks Grok Bot orders; Musk replies, "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon"
items.lead: Amazon is blocking orders placed by Grok Bot, as it does with other AI shopping agents, including Meta's Muse.
items.text: Amazon is blocking orders placed by Grok Bot, as it does with other AI shopping agents, including Meta's Muse. After an X user complained on 15 October that Grok Bot could not complete an Amazon order, Elon Musk replied, "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon." There was no new Grok Bot or Cursor changelog entry and nothing new on x.ai/news since the last edition. SpaceX reports third-quarter results on 20 October.

items.headline: Texas Monthly: state commission planned a closed-door talk on selling Boca Chica State Park; SpaceX named as buyer (unconfirmed)
items.lead: Texas Monthly reported on 16 October that the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission had planned a closed-door discussion on 5 November about selling the 1,300-acre Boca Chica State Park next to SpaceX's Starbase.
items.text: Texas Monthly reported on 16 October that the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission had planned a closed-door discussion on 5 November about selling the 1,300-acre Boca Chica State Park next to SpaceX's Starbase. Two unnamed sources told the magazine that SpaceX would be the buyer; this is unconfirmed. A department spokeswoman, Stephanie Garcia, said the commission "is not considering the sale of the Boca Chica property at its November meeting." SpaceX has asked the Federal Aviation Administration to raise the permitted launches from Starbase from 25 to 456 a year.

items.headline: Swinney: "The referendum campaign on Scottish independence has already begun"
items.lead: In his speech to the SNP conference in Aberdeen on 17 October, First Minister John Swinney said the independence referendum campaign "has already begun" and launched a "Choose Scotland" campaign; his spokesman said it starts with £100,000.
items.text: In his speech to the SNP conference in Aberdeen on 17 October, First Minister John Swinney said the independence referendum campaign "has already begun" and launched a "Choose Scotland" campaign; his spokesman said it starts with £100,000. The National says the campaign plans to survey 1.5 million Scots. Swinney cited a Survation poll for the Foundation for Reform (FoRE) with 54 percent for independence; other polls this week were mixed, with YouGov and More in Common showing a majority for staying in the United Kingdom. Referring to Manchester, he said, "Some think we should just be like Manchester ... Scotland is no city." He promised public control of buses before 2031, extension of the £2 bus fare cap to Aberdeen from April, a misogyny bill by June 2027 and a £30 million "Scotland Together" fund. Labour's Jackie Baillie called the speech "thin and threadbare"; Conservative leader Russell Findlay also criticized it. The SNP has about 51,000 members.

items.headline: Council moves to buy the empty Lafayette Yard hotel with a $4 million state grant and hand it to a private redeveloper for $1
items.lead: Trenton City Council voted on 6 October to apply for a $4 million New Jersey Economic Development Authority grant to buy the former Lafayette Yard Marriott at 1 West Lafayette Street, the city's only downtown hotel, empty since the state closed it for safety violations in 2017.
items.text: Trenton City Council voted on 6 October to apply for a $4 million New Jersey Economic Development Authority grant to buy the former Lafayette Yard Marriott at 1 West Lafayette Street, the city's only downtown hotel, empty since the state closed it for safety violations in 2017. Mayor Reed Gusciora told the Trentonian that the city would buy the building from its current owner with the grant and sell it for $1 to the designated redeveloper, Tetrabilt of South Carolina, which he said has committed to spend $20 million to reopen it, with long-term housing on the top two floors and a hotel below. The grant was first announced in November 2024; the mayor blamed the delay on procedural requirements, and the Trenton Journal has reported a lawsuit by a former owner's partners who still claim the property. Central Jersey Media reported on 14 October that the plan is moving forward; final state approval is still needed. The money for the purchase is public; the renovation and operation would be private.

items.headline: Israel's ambassador: Colombia is considering joining the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance
items.lead: Israel's ambassador to Colombia, Vivian Aisen, told The Media Line that Foreign Ministers Gideon Sa'ar and Omar Bula discussed a possible Colombian application to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance during Bula's visit to Jerusalem.
items.text: Israel's ambassador to Colombia, Vivian Aisen, told The Media Line that Foreign Ministers Gideon Sa'ar and Omar Bula discussed a possible Colombian application to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance during Bula's visit to Jerusalem. No formal application has been announced; the claim rests on the ambassador's account. Colombia adopted the alliance's working definition of antisemitism in 2022 but is not a member or observer. The report, published by the Jerusalem Post on 17 October, also says the two governments completed an exchange of diplomatic notes on 13 October restoring their 2020 free-trade agreement, and that, according to Israel's Foreign Ministry, Colombia is the tenth country with an embassy in Jerusalem and the fourth in Latin America. Bula also announced a national initiative against antisemitism, to be prepared with Colombia's Jewish communities and advice from the US State Department's antisemitism envoy.

items.headline: Evening: Trump gives Netanyahu his 'Complete and Total Endorsement'; Eisenkot falls to about 47 percent on Polymarket
items.lead: In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon addressed 'To the Great People of Israel,' President Trump called Netanyahu a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' and wrote: 'Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election.' He tied the endorsement to Iran, warned that unless Iran changes course 'we will soon finish the job,' and wrote that if Israel chooses 'the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so.' Netanyahu thanked him.
items.text: In a Truth Social post on Sunday afternoon addressed 'To the Great People of Israel,' President Trump called Netanyahu a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' and wrote: 'Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election.' He tied the endorsement to Iran, warned that unless Iran changes course 'we will soon finish the job,' and wrote that if Israel chooses 'the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so.' Netanyahu thanked him. It is Trump's first public endorsement in this campaign, nine days before the 27 October vote. On Polymarket's 'next prime minister' market, Eisenkot stood at about 47 percent on Sunday evening, down from about 54 percent this morning, and Netanyahu at about 32 percent; Bennett was at about 14 percent. Whether the move was caused by the post is not known.

items.headline: Evening: Netanyahu says Ben-Gvir will 'unequivocally' be in his next government; Ben-Gvir says Netanyahu's office told European states the opposite
items.lead: Asked by reporters on Sunday whether the broad government he wants after the election would include Ben-Gvir's party, Netanyahu answered 'unequivocally' and said his wish to keep the Defense and National Security ministries in Likud is no sign of a different coalition: 'there is no doubt we will make the same coalition' (Arutz 7).
items.text: Asked by reporters on Sunday whether the broad government he wants after the election would include Ben-Gvir's party, Netanyahu answered 'unequivocally' and said his wish to keep the Defense and National Security ministries in Likud is no sign of a different coalition: 'there is no doubt we will make the same coalition' (Arutz 7). On Sunday evening Ben-Gvir said, citing what he called 'checked and verified information,' that the Prime Minister's Office had formally promised several EU states that he would not be in the next government, and linked it to talk in Likud of a broad government with Eisenkot (Arutz 7; Ynet). Likud called it 'false political spin.' He gave no evidence; it is his claim. Earlier, Netanyahu told Radio North that Channel 14 host Yinon Magal's description of Eisenkot as a 'monkey' was 'very inappropriate' and that he condemned it, while Ben-Gvir defended Magal and said the word was political, not ethnic (Arutz 7).

items.headline: Evening: Aoun asks France's Barrot for help against a security vacuum in the south when UNIFIL leaves
items.lead: President Joseph Aoun told visiting French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot in Baabda on Sunday that Lebanon still wants UNIFIL's mandate extended, but that if this is impossible it 'welcomes any arrangement that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and avoids placing the Lebanese Army in direct contact with the Israeli army' (Naharnet; the Times of Israel reported the same).
items.text: President Joseph Aoun told visiting French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot in Baabda on Sunday that Lebanon still wants UNIFIL's mandate extended, but that if this is impossible it 'welcomes any arrangement that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and avoids placing the Lebanese Army in direct contact with the Israeli army' (Naharnet; the Times of Israel reported the same). Barrot is in Beirut for two days. Separately, Army Radio reported, and Arutz 7 repeated, that the IDF is allowing Lebanese villagers, and Syrian workers they employ, to harvest olives inside the security strip it holds in south Lebanon, from Kfar Shouba to Alma al-Shaab, under army escort; the IDF said it allows the harvest 'in several Christian villages,' although Kfar Shouba is a Sunni Muslim village. EUSM Lebanon watch: no new Israeli official or unofficial reaction was found on Sunday.

items.headline: Evening: the first runoff debate is tonight on Band; poll averages show a technical tie with Lula gaining
items.lead: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro meet in their first runoff debate on Band at 8 p.m.
items.text: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro meet in their first runoff debate on Band at 8 p.m. Brasília time on Sunday (2 a.m. Monday in Israel), a week before the 25 October runoff (Valor). Poder360's compilation of the 13 latest national polls shows Flávio numerically ahead in 11 and Lula in one, mostly within the margin of error. Quórum's average of the 14 runoff polls released from 12 to 17 October gives Flávio 51.4 percent of valid votes and Lula 48.6 percent, a technical tie; Lula rose in every poll that was repeated during the week, while Flávio did not gain in any. Polymarket put Flávio at about 80 percent on Sunday evening.

items.headline: Evening: the 17 October toll rises to more than 2,000 arrests and more than 600 police, gendarmes and firefighters injured; a marcher dies after collapsing in Paris
items.lead: At midday on Sunday Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez raised the count to more than 2,000 arrests across France and more than 600 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters injured, figures he called provisional (BFMTV; franceinfo).
items.text: At midday on Sunday Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez raised the count to more than 2,000 arrests across France and more than 600 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters injured, figures he called provisional (BFMTV; franceinfo). Saturday evening's figures were 1,200 arrests and 150 injured. In Paris the police prefecture counted 855 arrests, a 'record,' and the prosecutor 557 people in custody, 381 adults, 151 minors and 25 of unknown age; Lyon counted 160 arrests. The retail federation FCD says about 1,500 shops were hit and the damage runs to hundreds of millions of euros (France 24, from AFP). A marcher collapsed on the Boulevard Magenta in Paris and died after cardiac arrest; his age and identity were not released (TF1 Info; Le Parisien). Near Lyon, a fire broke out on Saturday night in the Saint-Exupéry immigration detention center (CNews). A synagogue on rue Burnouf in the 19th arrondissement was broken into overnight and its rooms ransacked; community leaders lean toward a burglary, while police and the community security service SPCJ are checking for a link to the riots (Times of Israel, French edition). Nuñez will go to Marseille on Monday.

items.headline: Evening: new clashes and looting at Place de la République; Macron will speak at 8 p.m.; mayors to rally at town halls on Monday
items.lead: On Sunday afternoon an undeclared gathering at Place de la République in Paris turned into clashes between several hundred people and the police, and looting resumed nearby; the police sent in the CRS 8 riot unit (CNews; BFMTV).
items.text: On Sunday afternoon an undeclared gathering at Place de la République in Paris turned into clashes between several hundred people and the police, and looting resumed nearby; the police sent in the CRS 8 riot unit (CNews; BFMTV). President Macron met the prime minister and the ministers concerned at 5:30 p.m. and will address the nation at 8 p.m. Paris time (9 p.m. in Israel), after this update. The Association of Mayors of France called on mayors and councils to gather in front of town halls from noon on Monday. National Assembly President Yaël Braun-Pivet will propose a parliamentary inquiry into the violence and the police strategy, and parties from the RN to the Ecologists have called for Nuñez to resign (France 24, from AFP). The mayors of Paris and Limoges complained of too few police. Jordan Bardella (RN) spoke of 'a deadly alliance between the far left and the looters'; the CGT called for 'peaceful' mobilization to continue and named an inter-union day of strikes and marches on 5 November. Analysis, attributed: AFP writes that international media see the day as 'the twilight of Macronism' and as setting up a radical-left versus far-right duel for 2027. On Polymarket Le Pen stood at about 48 percent on Sunday evening, Philippe at about 20 and Lisnard at about 12. In the United States, Trump wrote on Truth Social that 'France is burning'.

items.headline: Evening: Musk says the SpaceX–Nvidia 'Star Mind' computer will reach volume production next year
items.lead: Elon Musk wrote on X on 15 October that the 'Star Mind' computer being co-engineered by SpaceX and Nvidia is 'far better than almost anyone expects and will reach volume production next year,' and Nvidia's Jensen Huang said on the BG2 podcast that the two engineering teams are designing a new server meant to put data centers in space (Benzinga, carried by Yahoo Finance on 17 October).
items.text: Elon Musk wrote on X on 15 October that the 'Star Mind' computer being co-engineered by SpaceX and Nvidia is 'far better than almost anyone expects and will reach volume production next year,' and Nvidia's Jensen Huang said on the BG2 podcast that the two engineering teams are designing a new server meant to put data centers in space (Benzinga, carried by Yahoo Finance on 17 October). These are company targets, not delivered results.

items.headline: Three Sunday polls: Kan has Yashar 23 and Likud 21; i24NEWS has Likud 25; Channel 14 has Netanyahu's bloc at exactly 61
items.lead: Three seat polls published on Sunday evening, 18 October, nine days before the vote, point in different directions.
items.text: Three seat polls published on Sunday evening, 18 October, nine days before the vote, point in different directions. Kan News (Kantar, Dudu Hasid; 554 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points) gives Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar 23 seats and Likud 21, each up one from last week; Bennett's Beyachad 12; the Democrats 9, their highest since early September; Otzma Yehudit, Shas, Yisrael Beytenu and the Joint List (Hadash–Ta'al–Balad) 8 each; Religious Zionism 7, up from 5; United Torah Judaism 7; Ra'am 5; and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists 4. Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael falls below the threshold at 3.1 percent. The Eisenkot bloc has 52 seats and the Netanyahu bloc 51, with the Arab parties at 13. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 43 to 35 percent as more suitable for prime minister (Netanyahu had 38 a week earlier); Netanyahu leads Bennett 38 to 34. Thirty percent of respondents said they had not yet decided how to vote. An i24NEWS poll by Direct Polls (Tzuriel Sharon; 525 respondents, margin of error 4.2 points) has Likud at 25, down two; Yashar 21; Beyachad 13; Otzma Yehudit 10, its first double-digit result in this series; the Democrats 9; United Torah Judaism, Shas and the Joint List 8 each; and Yisrael Beytenu, Religious Zionism and Ra'am 6 each. The coalition parties total 57, the Zionist opposition 49 and the Arab parties 14; Winter (2.9 percent) and the Reservists (2.4 percent) are out. A Channel 14 poll by Next Data (559 respondents, fielded 18 October) keeps Likud at 29 and raises Yashar from 20 to 22; Shas and Beyachad have 10 each; the Democrats and United Torah Judaism 8 each; Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit and the Joint List 7 each; Yisrael Beytenu and Ra'am 6 each. It puts the right-wing bloc at exactly 61, down one from Wednesday, and narrows Netanyahu's head-to-head lead over Eisenkot to 51–49. On Polymarket, Eisenkot stood at about 46 percent early on Monday, Israel time, Netanyahu at about 29.5 and Bennett at about 12.5 (about $48.5 million traded), against about 47, 32 and 14 on Sunday evening.

items.headline: Netanyahu presents a new security doctrine: 'The regime must fall, and I will bring it down'; Eisenkot calls it 'two hollow pages'
items.lead: On Sunday Netanyahu held a two-hour security briefing for Israeli reporters at his Jerusalem office, his first such in-person briefing since 7 October 2023; several outlets boycotted it (Times of Israel).
items.text: On Sunday Netanyahu held a two-hour security briefing for Israeli reporters at his Jerusalem office, his first such in-person briefing since 7 October 2023; several outlets boycotted it (Times of Israel). He presented an updated national security doctrine that puts preemptive offensive action ahead of containment, said bringing down Iran's regime remains the main goal ('The regime must fall, and I will bring it down'), claimed that about 90 percent of the work against Israel's enemies is done, and said Israel will act alone against Iran if necessary. He said he would put about NIS 450 billion into defense over the next decade, including more domestic weapons production (Ynet; Times of Israel). He warned that 'in two years' a U.S. president 'very hostile to Israel' could take office, and said Israel must build alliances with India and Latin America. On the next coalition he rejected a unity government with his opponents, said he wants a 'broad national government' that keeps his current partners, including Ben-Gvir's party, and said he would pass a Haredi enlistment law after the election. He called the international reaction to recent settler attacks 'a huge exaggeration' while saying the rioters cause Israel 'enormous damage.' Eisenkot answered that the doctrine was 'two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine' and an attempt to frighten voters (Ynet).

items.headline: Former chief rabbi Yitzhak Yosef rules it forbidden to vote for Otzma Yehudit; IDF weighs a leave freeze on election day
items.lead: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, the former Sephardi chief rabbi and a member of Shas's Council of Torah Sages, published a letter on Sunday ruling that it is forbidden under Jewish law to vote for Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, because Ben-Gvir goes up to the Temple Mount and encourages others to do so; he wrote that whoever votes for the party carries the sin (Arutz 7; Times of Israel).
items.text: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, the former Sephardi chief rabbi and a member of Shas's Council of Torah Sages, published a letter on Sunday ruling that it is forbidden under Jewish law to vote for Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, because Ben-Gvir goes up to the Temple Mount and encourages others to do so; he wrote that whoever votes for the party carries the sin (Arutz 7; Times of Israel). Shas and Otzma compete for some of the same religious right-wing voters; Otzma had between 7 and 10 seats in Sunday's three polls. Channel 12 (N12) reported on Sunday that Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir had decided to cancel leave for soldiers on election day, 27 October, because of concern about attacks meant to influence the vote. The IDF's own statement said an alert order had placed additional ground forces on standby and that a decision on leave 'has not yet been finalized' and would be made later this week (Times of Israel). Responding to Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu, Eisenkot said that 'Israel's citizens are the only ones who will decide,' told Channel 12 that he had asked in meetings that there be no intervention in Israel's election, and said the leader of the largest party should be 'the natural candidate' for prime minister. Trump told Axios, as quoted by the Times of Israel, 'I was always going to do that. I just didn't want to do it too soon.'

sources.name: The Times of Israel (live blog, 18 October)

items.headline: Before the Tampa talks: Lebanon's demands, Netanyahu's verdict on the army's pilot zones, and a Hezbollah defense of arms transfers
items.lead: The US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa is set for Tuesday, 20 October.
items.text: The US–Lebanon–Israel military meeting at US Central Command in Tampa is set for Tuesday, 20 October. According to Arab media cited by Israel Hayom, Lebanon's delegation has been told to seek a halt to Israeli air strikes and bulldozer work in border villages, a timetable for Israeli withdrawal, wider Lebanese army deployment along the border, procedures for withdrawal and handover, and a mechanism for handling violations; Beirut also wants its army to be the only body that carries out security checks and disarmament. Netanyahu told reporters on Sunday that Israel had let the Lebanese army show it could clear Hezbollah infrastructure in two pilot areas, but that it had 'not demonstrated sufficient capabilities,' and that Israel would do the job itself if the army cannot (Times of Israel; not found in a second report). Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah, speaking in Tibnin on Sunday, defended the group's right to move weapons to the front: 'How will it fight this enemy? Are we supposed to fight with bags of potatoes?' (L'Orient Today; not independently confirmed). After Army Radio reported on Sunday that the IDF allows olive picking inside its security strip, residents of the Arqoub villages refused to go to their groves near Kfar Shouba on the IDF's terms, which, according to Lebanese reports, included handing over phones and ID cards, a limit of 100 people and 25 vehicles, and no Lebanese army or UNIFIL escort; the head of the Kfar Shouba municipality said an Israeli patrol then ordered farmers in another area to leave (L'Orient Today; Lebanon Times). No IDF account of these conditions was found.

items.headline: EUSM Lebanon watch: Ireland's government moves to take part; still no Israeli reaction
items.lead: Ireland's government has said it wants to contribute to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon.
items.text: Ireland's government has said it wants to contribute to the EU Support Mission in Lebanon. Foreign Affairs and Defence Minister Helen McEntee said on 12 October that the coalition wants Ireland to 'participate fully in any European mission to Lebanon' and would bring forward legislation to remove the 'Triple Lock' requirement of UN Security Council approval for sending more than 12 Irish troops abroad (Highland Radio). RTÉ reported on 18 October that the bill is now before the Oireachtas, that opposition parties strongly oppose it as a threat to Irish neutrality, and that the exact nature of the mission's military component is still unclear. Ireland's last UNIFIL contingent, about 300 soldiers, deploys next month, and McEntee has said Irish forces will be out of south Lebanon entirely by Easter. No decision to send Irish personnel to the EU mission has been taken. The contributors reported earlier are Italy, France and Spain. No new official or unofficial Israeli reaction to the mission was found from Sunday evening to early Monday, in Hebrew or English media, in statements by the Foreign Ministry, the Prime Minister's Office or the IDF, or on X.

items.headline: Electricity Authority caps each new data center at 200 megawatts; reports differ on the national ceiling
items.lead: The plenum of Israel's Electricity Authority decided on Sunday evening, 18 October, that each new data center may connect to the grid at no more than 200 megawatts, and that developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, or NIS 400 million for a full 200-megawatt site, to keep out speculative applications (Globes; TheMarker).
items.text: The plenum of Israel's Electricity Authority decided on Sunday evening, 18 October, that each new data center may connect to the grid at no more than 200 megawatts, and that developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, or NIS 400 million for a full 200-megawatt site, to keep out speculative applications (Globes; TheMarker). The two papers differ on the total. Globes reports a ceiling of 1,300 megawatts for the whole sector, of which 300 megawatts must serve local users and the rest may serve foreign buyers of computing power. TheMarker reports a proposed ceiling of 3 gigawatts plus 300 megawatts reserved for the defense establishment, and says half of each guarantee would be returned only after 60 percent of the requested capacity is operating. TheMarker says the details had not yet been fully published, and the authority's own text was not found online, so the overall ceiling is unconfirmed. Other criteria, including a split between the center of the country and the periphery and preferences for developers who bring their own generation and storage, go to public comment; Globes expects the first new approvals to take at least several months, probably until after a new government is formed, and notes that more than one gigawatt of data centers was already approved under the earlier first-come policy. Requests submitted to the grid operator total about 27,000 megawatts, against a record peak demand of about 17,300 megawatts in August 2025; the freeze on new applications above 8 megawatts ends in early December (Bizportal).

items.headline: Macron speaks of "anger and shame," promises the looters will pay, but declares no state of emergency and offers no new measures
items.lead: President Macron addressed the nation for about nine minutes at 8 p.m. Paris time on 18 October (9 p.m. in Israel), saying, "We all feel anger and shame tonight."
items.text: President Macron addressed the nation for about nine minutes at 8 p.m. Paris time on 18 October (9 p.m. in Israel), saying, "We all feel anger and shame tonight." He blamed the violence of 17 October on "agitators from ultra-left groups, joined by many delinquents" and said "nothing explains it, nothing excuses it"; those who destroyed "must pay," those who looted "must repay," and the state will be "intractable." He said prefects, together with mayors, may go as far as banning some gatherings, ordered "transparency" on the policing strategy and told Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to "draw all the lessons" on intelligence and anticipation. A crisis cell will help shopkeepers and local governments from Monday. He asked parties and unions to condemn the violence "without ambiguity" and said, "The country needs order... not escalation" and "Our country deserves a fine presidential election in six months." He said he understood high school pupils and students and that a youth consultation platform has received more than 100,000 contributions, but he announced no new cost-of-living measures; the prime minister is to meet parties, unions and local officials. He did not declare a state of emergency, which the right had demanded, and he keeps his trip to four Gulf countries from Monday to Wednesday. France 24, citing AFP, noted that he said nothing about the protesters who were badly injured.

sources.name: Élysée: address to the French people, 18 Oct

items.headline: Bardella calls the address "lamentable," Retailleau asks again for a state of emergency, Philippe wants decisions; LFI calls it "irresponsible"
items.lead: Candidates on the right and left criticized the address.
items.text: Candidates on the right and left criticized the address. Jordan Bardella (RN) called it a "lamentable address" from a "cowardly and disoriented" government; earlier on Sunday he had said Macron should "ask forgiveness and go." Marine Le Pen, in a televised statement before the address, spoke of "a deep crisis of confidence and authority" and a Macron government "out of breath, exhausted, disoriented," and blamed La France insoumise and "its armed wing, the antifa groups." Bruno Retailleau (LR) wrote on X that the address was "very worrying," that Macron "appears totally overwhelmed," and asked him again to declare a state of emergency. Édouard Philippe wrote on X that he had heard "a laudable wish to restore dialogue" but would have preferred decisions to restore order, saying the country "needs to be led" ("a besoin d'être commandé"). Éric Ciotti said Macron had "spoken to say nothing" and asked the national anti-terrorism prosecutor to take up the case. On the left, LFI's Manuel Bompard called the address "absolutely irresponsible" and Mathilde Panot called Macron an "artisan of chaos"; Marine Tondelier (Ecologists) said she was "very disappointed" that he said nothing about the injured protesters; Fabien Roussel said there were no answers in eight and a half minutes. CGT leader Sophie Binet told AFP that Macron "has understood nothing." Jean-Luc Mélenchon, on LCI on Sunday evening, said a curfew or state of emergency "are not solutions," accused Nuñez and the police chiefs of "total incompetence," and set three demands for Prime Minister Lecornu: a price freeze, the abolition of the Parcoursup university-admission platform and public compensation for the shopkeepers who were hit. Éric Zemmour proposed "remigration" for rioters with dual nationality (BFMTV).

items.headline: Final 17 October toll: 2,397 arrests and 997 police and gendarmes injured; more looting in Paris on Sunday night; curfew for minors in Guadeloupe
items.lead: The Interior Ministry's consolidated count for 17 October is 2,397 arrests and 997 police officers and gendarmes injured, seven of them seriously (BFMTV; RFI), up from the provisional 2,000 arrests and 600 injured given at midday on Sunday.
items.text: The Interior Ministry's consolidated count for 17 October is 2,397 arrests and 997 police officers and gendarmes injured, seven of them seriously (BFMTV; RFI), up from the provisional 2,000 arrests and 600 injured given at midday on Sunday. Looting went on in Paris on Sunday evening: the police made 108 arrests during the day, 66 of them in the evening; at least five shops were looted, including a Darty electronics store in Belleville and two supermarkets; the door of the BHV Marais department store was broken and looters got inside; and barricades were set on fire on the Boulevard Voltaire (20 Minutes, from AFP). Attempted break-ins were also reported in Lyon, Marseille and near Nantes. In Guadeloupe, after looting and fires in Pointe-à-Pitre and Les Abymes on the night of 17 to 18 October in which three police officers were wounded by gunfire, the prefect, Thierry Devimeux, imposed a curfew on unaccompanied minors from 8 p.m. Sunday to 6 a.m. Monday (Le Figaro, from AFP; France-Antilles; Outre-mer La 1ère). In Mulhouse a 17-year-old girl permanently lost her left eye on 17 October; witnesses speak of a tear-gas grenade, and the prosecutor, Nicolas Heitz, has given the inquiry to the police inspectorate (IGPN) (France 3; RTL). According to Le Figaro's live coverage, not independently confirmed: Bordeaux had a record 109 people in custody, 38 of them minors; the Marseille prefecture spoke of 30,000 looters, a figure Mayor Benoît Payan called "far-fetched"; and about 7,000 people, by the city's estimate, marched in Limoges on Sunday evening after the town hall fire.

items.headline: Ifop's Dabi: the riots could strengthen Le Pen's first-round base; no post-riot poll yet; Polymarket steady
items.lead: Frédéric Dabi, director general of Ifop, told AFP on 18 October that the risk of a flare-up six months before a presidential election is "totally unprecedented" under the Fifth Republic; he said the chaos of 17 October could "strengthen Marine Le Pen's first-round electoral base" and make it harder for Jean-Luc Mélenchon to reach the runoff, but urged caution about the effect at the polls (Sud Ouest; Midi Libre).
items.text: Frédéric Dabi, director general of Ifop, told AFP on 18 October that the risk of a flare-up six months before a presidential election is "totally unprecedented" under the Fifth Republic; he said the chaos of 17 October could "strengthen Marine Le Pen's first-round electoral base" and make it harder for Jean-Luc Mélenchon to reach the runoff, but urged caution about the effect at the polls (Sud Ouest; Midi Libre). No poll taken after 17 October has been published yet. On Polymarket (about $153 million traded) Le Pen was at about 48 percent early on 19 October, Philippe 19.5, Lisnard 12, Mélenchon 9.5 and Glucksmann 4.5, almost unchanged from Sunday evening. On Monday the mayors' association holds rallies at town halls at noon, Commerce Minister Serge Papin meets retail federations, banks and insurers, and Nuñez goes to Marseille; on Tuesday National Assembly President Yaël Braun-Pivet is to propose a commission of inquiry, and the Assembly is still scheduled to vote on the first part of the 2027 budget the same day (Le Figaro live; Assembly calendar).

items.headline: First runoff debate: Lula and Flávio trade corruption charges; Flávio admits his father's government fell short on health
items.lead: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their first runoff debate, on Band on the evening of 18 October (it began about 15 minutes late and ended about 10:15 p.m. Brasília time, 4:15 a.m. Monday in Israel).
items.text: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their first runoff debate, on Band on the evening of 18 October (it began about 15 minutes late and ended about 10:15 p.m. Brasília time, 4:15 a.m. Monday in Israel). Flávio raised the INSS pension fraud and the names of Roberta Luchsinger and Lula's son Fábio Luís ("Lulinha"); Lula raised the Banco Master case and money from its owner, Daniel Vorcaro, for a film about Jair Bolsonaro, and told the Bolsonaros, over Eduardo Bolsonaro's campaign in the United States, "You are betraying the homeland" (Exame). In one exchange Flávio asked whether "60 percent of prisoners voted for you"; Lula answered, "I want 100 percent, including your father." Flávio admitted that health "was not the best result" of his father's government and said, "I make my mea culpa here" (O Globo); he promised a public health service "of Einstein standard," a "war on the PCC as narco-terrorists," a Ministry of Prosperity and a plan to buy household and business debts from the banks. O Globo columnist Míriam Leitão wrote that Lula had the advantage in the second block and that Flávio's debt plan recycles the government's own Desenrola program. In the third block Lula challenged Flávio to open his bank and phone records to the heads of the Supreme Court and the Electoral Court "so that the Brazilian people can find out who the thief is"; Flávio replied, "Your money is always off the books" (Band; CartaCapital). Political scientists quoted by Valor expect little effect on votes, since Quaest found 91 percent and Datafolha 93 percent of voters say their choice is final. On Polymarket (about $188 million traded) Flávio was at about 78.5 percent early on 19 October, down from about 80 on Sunday evening, and Lula at 20.5. New polls registered with the electoral court for release from 19 October include AtlasIntel (13 to 18 October, 5,000 interviews) and PoderData; Quaest is due on 21 October and Datafolha on 22 October. The runoff is on 25 October.

items.headline: Health-tech startup MyMonitor.AI moves its headquarters from Philadelphia to downtown Trenton
items.lead: MyMonitor.AI, a health-care artificial intelligence startup, has moved its headquarters from Philadelphia to Suite 202 at 1 West State Street in downtown Trenton; Mayor Reed Gusciora joined founder and chief executive Charles Mbata for a ribbon cutting on 13 October (Trenton Journal, from a city release; Quadratín).
items.text: MyMonitor.AI, a health-care artificial intelligence startup, has moved its headquarters from Philadelphia to Suite 202 at 1 West State Street in downtown Trenton; Mayor Reed Gusciora joined founder and chief executive Charles Mbata for a ribbon cutting on 13 October (Trenton Journal, from a city release; Quadratín). The company was one of 13 in the first Trenton group of the Novella Center for Entrepreneurship's Conscious Venture Lab, a free 14-week accelerator that began in October 2025. Government role: the accelerator is paid for by a City of Trenton grant from its federal Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery Fund money (Community News, May 2025); no public subsidy to the company itself has been reported, and no job numbers were given. The ribbon cutting took place before the last edition but had not been reported here.
