items.headline: Grok Bot update: company says computer tasks finish three times faster; The Grid Fin reports X Chat access and new finance connectors
items.lead: The Grok Bot account announced on X on 16 October an update to "quality, polish, and speed": it says computer tasks now finish three times sooner on average and other replies arrive in less than half the time, chat cards have a cleaner design, voice calls are faster and better at remembering past conversations, email supports plus aliases for routines, tagging @bot in an X post starts a task, and notifications go only to the device in use.
items.text: The Grok Bot account announced on X on 16 October an update to "quality, polish, and speed": it says computer tasks now finish three times sooner on average and other replies arrive in less than half the time, chat cards have a cleaner design, voice calls are faster and better at remembering past conversations, email supports plus aliases for routines, tagging @bot in an X post starts a task, and notifications go only to the device in use. The Grid Fin reports that the same update lets Grok Bot read a user's X Chat messages once X is connected, announced by Paul Vann, and adds connectors including Robinhood, Coinbase, Trello, PostHog, beehiiv and eToro; those additions are not independently confirmed here. The company has not said how it measured the speed gain, and the official changelog still lists version 0.70.2 of 11 October as the latest release.

items.headline: Before Tuesday's results, analysts expect SpaceX's first quarterly profit as a listed company
items.lead: SpaceX reports third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, 20 October, with an audio webcast at 4:30 p.m. New York time (11:30 p.m. in Israel); it is the first report to include Cursor, bought in August (TECHi).
items.text: SpaceX reports third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, 20 October, with an audio webcast at 4:30 p.m. New York time (11:30 p.m. in Israel); it is the first report to include Cursor, bought in August (TECHi). According to TipRanks, analysts expect earnings of $0.14 a share, against a loss of $0.09 in the second quarter, and revenue of $12.89 billion, against $7.81 billion; Evercore ISI raised its price target to $275 from $230 on 16 October. The consensus figures come from TipRanks and are not independently confirmed. SPCX closed Friday at $146.03, down 1.7 percent on the day and, by TECHi's count, 15.1 percent below its 6 October close.

items.headline: Andreessen posts an original film comment on X: "At long last, movies are back"
items.lead: On 18 October 2026 at 8:01 a.m. Israel time, Marc Andreessen wrote on X: "YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING, PRIMETIME, and DIGGER make 2026 the best year for film since 2015 (SICARIO, EX MACHINA, and MAD MAX: FURY ROAD). At long last, movies are back."
items.text: On 18 October 2026 at 8:01 a.m. Israel time, Marc Andreessen wrote on X: "YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING, PRIMETIME, and DIGGER make 2026 the best year for film since 2015 (SICARIO, EX MACHINA, and MAD MAX: FURY ROAD). At long last, movies are back." It is his first original post found since his 4 October recommendation of DIGGER, and X showed about 528,000 views by the morning of 19 October. All of his other posts from 16 to 19 October were reposts, chiefly AI-made videos tied to the Sloptoberfest contest. His total X post count rose by 19 posts in the three days to 19 October, about 6 a day, which is roughly a quarter of his pre-July rate of about 25 a day.

items.headline: Gantz pulls Blue and White out of the race; Sa'ar and Smotrich press Winter to follow, and he refuses
items.lead: Benny Gantz announced on Monday afternoon, 19 October, that his Blue and White party will not run in the 27 October election, reversing his statement a week earlier that he would stay in the race 'no matter what' (Ynet; Israel Hayom; Jerusalem Post).
items.text: Benny Gantz announced on Monday afternoon, 19 October, that his Blue and White party will not run in the 27 October election, reversing his statement a week earlier that he would stay in the race 'no matter what' (Ynet; Israel Hayom; Jerusalem Post). Polls had put the party at about 1 percent, far below the 3.25 percent threshold. Gantz said he would 'continue fighting for unity' and for a broad Zionist government. Because the withdrawal comes so late, the party stays on the ballot, but votes for it will be wasted (Times of Israel). A source close to Gantz told Ynet the timing was set so that soldiers, who begin voting on Tuesday, 20 October, would not waste their votes; Israel Hayom's sources said he was promised nothing in return. Eisenkot, Golan and Lapid praised the decision, and Yoaz Hendel asked Gantz's voters to move to his Reservists list. On the right, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar urged right-wing parties below or near the threshold to withdraw, citing the 1992 election, when, he said, wasted right-wing votes let the left reach 61 seats; Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called on Ofer Winter to 'take responsibility' (Jerusalem Post). Winter said Amcha Yisrael will run 'until the end,' and Noam's Avi Maoz and the Haredi Public party's Moti Leitner also said they will stay in (Channel 14; Jerusalem Post).

items.headline: Three Monday polls: Channel 12 has Eisenkot's bloc 55–51; Channel 13 has it 51–50; Channel 14 gives the right 62
items.lead: Three seat polls published on Monday evening, 19 October, eight days before the vote, again disagree.
items.text: Three seat polls published on Monday evening, 19 October, eight days before the vote, again disagree. Channel 12 (Midgam, Mano Geva, with iPanel; 507 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points) gives Yashar 24 seats, Likud 21, Bennett's Beyachad 14, the Democrats and the Joint List 9 each, Yisrael Beytenu, Shas and Otzma Yehudit 8 each, Religious Zionism and United Torah Judaism 7 each and Ra'am 5; Winter's Amcha Yisrael (2.8 percent) and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists (2.1 percent) fall below the threshold. That puts Eisenkot's bloc at 55 and Netanyahu's at 51, with the Arab parties at 14. Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 45 to 33 percent as preferred prime minister. Sixty-four percent said Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu did not affect their chance of voting Likud, 12 percent said it made it more likely and 17 percent less likely; 64 percent opposed Yinon Magal's description of Eisenkot as a 'monkey' (Times of Israel; Walla; Haaretz). Channel 13 (Madad, Shmuel Rosner and Noah Slepkov; 1,016 respondents, margin of error 3.1 points, fielded Sunday) keeps Yashar at 20 and Likud at 18, raises Beyachad from 12 to 14, and has both Winter and the Reservists in with 4 seats each; Eisenkot's bloc has 51, Netanyahu's 50 and the Arab parties 15, a reversal of last week's 51–50 for Netanyahu (Haaretz; Walla; Maariv). Channel 14 (Next Data; 454 adults, 19 October) has Likud at 30, up one, and Yashar at 19, down three, and gives the right-wing bloc 62 seats, the Zionist opposition 45 and the Arab parties 13; Netanyahu leads Eisenkot 54 to 46 head to head (Channel 14; Ice). The Channel 12 and 13 polls were taken at least partly before Gantz withdrew. On Polymarket, Eisenkot stood at about 50 percent early on Tuesday, Israel time, Netanyahu at about 28, Bennett at about 13 and Lieberman at about 4 (about $49.1 million traded), against about 46, 29.5 and 12.5 on Monday morning.

items.headline: Channel 12: Netanyahu aide Urich told police he kept working for Qatar into 2024; Bennett calls it treason
items.lead: Channel 12 reported on Monday evening, citing transcripts of his questioning by the police unit Lahav 433, that Netanyahu's adviser Jonatan Urich admitted he kept working with Qatari clients until at least mid-2024, months after the 7 October 2023 attack, and was paid hundreds of thousands of shekels (Channel 12; Ynet; Times of Israel).
items.text: Channel 12 reported on Monday evening, citing transcripts of his questioning by the police unit Lahav 433, that Netanyahu's adviser Jonatan Urich admitted he kept working with Qatari clients until at least mid-2024, months after the 7 October 2023 attack, and was paid hundreds of thousands of shekels (Channel 12; Ynet; Times of Israel). Asked whether he worked for Qatar after 7 October, he answered, 'Certainly, not in Israel'; asked whether he told Netanyahu, he said, 'I don't report to the prime minister about things I do,' and that as an outside adviser he was never required to disclose such work. He denies promoting Qatar inside Israel. Netanyahu has testified that he knew of no link between his aides and Qatar. Naftali Bennett called the affair 'the gravest case of treason in the history of the State of Israel' and demanded that Netanyahu, who still employs Urich, explain 'what is going on between you and Qatar' (Times of Israel). The report rests on transcripts aired by Channel 12; no response from Netanyahu's office to this report was found.

items.headline: Tampa talks open Tuesday; Lebanon says it will refuse direct army-to-army coordination with Israel
items.lead: Lebanese and Israeli military delegations meet on Tuesday and Wednesday, 20 and 21 October, at US Central Command in Tampa, with US Marine Corps Major General Joseph Clearfield leading the American side, according to official Lebanese sources quoted by LBCI and Naharnet; earlier reports had said the talks would run to 22 October.
items.text: Lebanese and Israeli military delegations meet on Tuesday and Wednesday, 20 and 21 October, at US Central Command in Tampa, with US Marine Corps Major General Joseph Clearfield leading the American side, according to official Lebanese sources quoted by LBCI and Naharnet; earlier reports had said the talks would run to 22 October. L'Orient Today reports that Washington and Israel have set direct coordination between the two armies as the condition for the talks to move forward, and that political negotiations are off the table for now. Lebanese officials told The National that Beirut will reject that: 'There are Israelis and Lebanese, with the Americans in the middle. That's it and that's how it will remain.' A Lebanese military source said no decision to expand the pilot zones or set up a verification mechanism is expected, and officials said they expect little progress before Israel's election. According to LBCI, the Lebanese side will say Israel has not respected the terms of the first pilot zone, including strikes, re-entry into the area and the killing of a Lebanese civilian. Netanyahu said on Sunday that Israel will stay in its zone in south Lebanon as long as Hezbollah is not disarmed (The National). MTV's correspondent in Tampa reported that the first day will review the pilot zones and run from 4 p.m. to 11 p.m. Beirut time (5 p.m. to midnight Israel time); that schedule is from MTV only and is unconfirmed.

items.headline: Beirut: army steps up patrols after Hezbollah supporters block a police raid; Aoun orders a ban on armed demonstrations
items.lead: The Lebanese army has increased patrols and set up temporary checkpoints in Beirut and its southern suburbs after a rise in tension with Hezbollah supporters (The National; L'Orient Today).
items.text: The Lebanese army has increased patrols and set up temporary checkpoints in Beirut and its southern suburbs after a rise in tension with Hezbollah supporters (The National; L'Orient Today). The tension follows the 5 October seizure of 500 kilograms of explosives at Dahr al-Baidar, which Hezbollah says are its own, and a police raid last Friday on a warehouse of spoiled medicines in the Gallerie Semaan district, where, according to the Internal Security Forces, young men on motorcycles tried to stop the force from entering; the army was sent in to calm the situation. Hezbollah said the police entered 'without following the agreed procedures.' Prime Minister Nawaf Salam wrote on X on Sunday that he had asked the justice minister and the attorney general to widen the explosives investigation and to arrest everyone involved in possessing or transporting illegal weapons, and repeated that the decision of war and peace must belong to the state alone. On Monday President Joseph Aoun called at a security meeting for a ban on armed demonstrations, the seizure of weapons and the referral of violators to court (L'Orient Today). Hezbollah's parliamentary leader Mohammad Raad accused officials of submitting to the enemy's 'dictates,' and MP Ibrahim Moussawi warned of an 'imminent explosion' in the streets (L'Orient Today; the MPs' statements were not found in a second report).

items.headline: Data center rules: about 1,300 new megawatts until 2030, NIS 2 million guarantees, and a separate plan to give sites land without tenders
items.lead: Fuller reports on the Electricity Authority's 18 October decision explain the difference between earlier accounts.
items.text: Fuller reports on the Electricity Authority's 18 October decision explain the difference between earlier accounts. Beyond about 2,000 megawatts of connections already approved, the authority will allocate about 1,300 new megawatts until 2030: about 1,000 for large commercial data centers and about 300 for the government, bringing the total to roughly 3,000 to 3,300 megawatts, which Calcalist says equals about 20 percent of Israel's projected electricity use in 2030 (Calcalist/Ctech; Globes). Each new site is capped at 200 megawatts; developers must post guarantees of NIS 2 million per megawatt, and sites must have backup arrangements that let them be cut off from the grid at times of extreme demand. The full decision will be published in the coming days for three weeks of public comment and may change. Avi Shkouri of Psagot told Globes that only about 4 percent of open requests can be met, and that the largest planned projects, including Mega DC in Hadera (about 1,100 megawatts), Kidmat Galil and Nesher (875) and Neve Yamin (720), will have to be redesigned or split. Globes also reports that at a meeting at the Government Secretariat with Economy Minister Nir Barkat, Cabinet Secretary Yossi Fuchs and Erez Askal of the national AI directorate, officials agreed to advance recognizing data centers as productive industry in national priority areas, so they could receive state land without a tender at a set price; the Finance Ministry's budget division says it did not agree, and the Economy Ministry says the decision is not final. The land plan is reported only by Globes and is unconfirmed.

items.headline: SCMP: US and Chinese negotiators push for investment deals before the November Trump–Xi meeting in Shenzhen; China adds export controls on drones and tunnel borers
items.lead: The South China Morning Post reported on 20 October, citing several unnamed sources, that US and Chinese negotiators have made 'considerable progress' on setting up a joint Board of Investment ahead of Trump and Xi's planned meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, modeled on the Board of Trade led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Vice Premier He Lifeng.
items.text: The South China Morning Post reported on 20 October, citing several unnamed sources, that US and Chinese negotiators have made 'considerable progress' on setting up a joint Board of Investment ahead of Trump and Xi's planned meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen in November, modeled on the Board of Trade led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Vice Premier He Lifeng. According to the report, the sides are discussing a shortlist of possible Chinese investments in non-sensitive US sectors such as electric vehicles, battery storage and power equipment, or possibly consumer goods; one source said the remaining issues have 'major gaps.' The paper also reports that both sides are using leverage, rare earths for China and jet engine and aircraft parts for the United States, in talks on extending the trade truce, which now runs to January 2027. These points rest on anonymous sources and are not independently confirmed. Separately, on 19 October China's commerce ministry issued two announcements, effective 18 November, that require export licenses for long-range and long-endurance drones and key drone parts, and for tunnel boring machines, some excavators and high-altitude shotcrete machines bound for 'sensitive countries and regions' in disputes with China; the notices do not name those destinations (Anadolu; Peter's World, citing the ministry's announcements). No US government response had been published.

items.headline: EU presents its Arctic strategy today, with a secure undersea cable to Greenland; Nuuk's vote on the US defense agreement is set for 3 November
items.lead: The European Commission is due to present a new Arctic strategy on Tuesday, 20 October, and drafts seen by Euronews and AFP say the EU will connect Greenland to Europe with a 'sovereign and secure submarine cable' and work on a longer-term cable from Europe through Greenland and Canada to Japan (Euronews also names South Korea).
items.text: The European Commission is due to present a new Arctic strategy on Tuesday, 20 October, and drafts seen by Euronews and AFP say the EU will connect Greenland to Europe with a 'sovereign and secure submarine cable' and work on a longer-term cable from Europe through Greenland and Canada to Japan (Euronews also names South Korea). The drafts also propose joint procurement or pooling of icebreakers, including nuclear-powered ones, an Arctic cable hub with Norway and Iceland to monitor and repair undersea cables, and better surveillance of the Russian 'shadow fleet' (Euronews; AFP via France 24). According to AFP, the draft never names Trump, mentions the United States only as a possible participant in a regular summit of 'Nordic neighborhood' partners, and adds no new money beyond the €200 million for Greenland that Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced in September; Euronews reports that €107 million of EU funds is already earmarked for connectivity projects involving Greenland. These details come from drafts and may change in the final text. In Nuuk, the agenda of Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, lists the second reading of the 22 September US–Denmark–Greenland defense agreement for 3 November; the agreement also needs the Danish parliament's consent before it can take effect (Inatsisartut; 2eu.brussels).

items.headline: BDRC releases Yigdzin, a free open model for reading Tibetan texts
items.lead: The Buddhist Digital Resource Center (BDRC) in Boston has released Yigdzin, an open OCR model that converts scanned Tibetan pages into searchable text, announced on 16 October and not reported here before.
items.text: The Buddhist Digital Resource Center (BDRC) in Boston has released Yigdzin, an open OCR model that converts scanned Tibetan pages into searchable text, announced on 16 October and not reported here before. It reads both the dbu can and dbu med scripts in woodblock prints, manuscripts and modern books, is free to use at ocr.bdrc.io, and is published under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face (BDRC; Hugging Face model card). According to BDRC's own model card, the 810-million-parameter model was built by Élie Roux and Eric Werner on Baidu's PaddleOCR-VL, has a median character error rate of about 1.4 percent on a 1,070-page test set, and is being applied to about 25 million scanned pages; these figures are BDRC's and have not been tested independently. BDRC will present the model in a public webinar on 28 October. The work was funded by the Khyentse Foundation.

items.headline: Nuñez offers to resign and Macron refuses; first local curfews in Paris, Lyon, Nice, the Lille area and Bordeaux
items.lead: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation after Macron's address on the evening of 18 October, and the Élysée said on Monday morning that the president refused it because of 'the need for continuous command of the police,' while asking for 'new methods of action' against rioters (franceinfo; BFMTV; Le Parisien).
items.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation after Macron's address on the evening of 18 October, and the Élysée said on Monday morning that the president refused it because of 'the need for continuous command of the police,' while asking for 'new methods of action' against rioters (franceinfo; BFMTV; Le Parisien). Nuñez told France Inter, 'I am responsible for everything that happens,' and admitted a 'lack of anticipation' and a 'loss of control' in some cities; Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said on France 2, 'We incontestably failed' (TF1 Info live). After a crisis meeting Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced three decisions: a 'massive' penal response, partial and local curfews ordered by prefects, and support for businesses, with 100 percent state-paid partial unemployment and a special fund; the government says at least 3,000 shops were damaged or looted over the weekend. He said he would not put all of Paris under curfew and that a state of emergency remains possible 'if it is useful.' The curfews on Monday night: in Paris, the central esplanade of the Place de la République and streets leading into Les Halles from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with demonstrations banned from 8 p.m. in République, Châtelet, Bastille, the main railway stations, the Champs-Élysées and around the Élysée, Matignon and Parliament; in Lyon, the city center from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.; in Nice, a curfew for minors from 9 p.m. until 25 October, ordered by Mayor Éric Ciotti; in Lille, Douai, Denain and Wattignies, a curfew for unaccompanied minors from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Monday and Tuesday nights; and in Bordeaux, for unaccompanied minors from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m., from 20 to 26 October (Le Parisien; TF1 Info; franceinfo). Le Parisien's reporters described a calm first night in Paris, with gendarmes sealing the Forum des Halles and a police helicopter overhead; ABC of Madrid also reported calm. In Lyon, about 100 members of the ultra-right joined a rally in support of shopkeepers and chanted slogans such as 'Islam out of Europe' (Le Progrès, as quoted by Le Parisien). Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said the curfew 'must remain exceptional.'

items.headline: Courts: 2,513 people in custody and 67 jailed; looters to be charged as organized crime; antiterrorism prosecutors weigh the Limoges fire
items.lead: Darmanin said on TF1's evening news on 19 October that 2,513 people had been placed in police custody since Saturday and 67 had already been jailed, 34 of them in the Aix-Marseille appeals court area, with sentences of up to five years; he has told all prosecutors to treat looters as organized crime, which allows custody of up to 72 hours instead of 48 and the use of phone taps and location tracking (TF1 Info; Le Parisien).
items.text: Darmanin said on TF1's evening news on 19 October that 2,513 people had been placed in police custody since Saturday and 67 had already been jailed, 34 of them in the Aix-Marseille appeals court area, with sentences of up to five years; he has told all prosecutors to treat looters as organized crime, which allows custody of up to 72 hours instead of 48 and the use of phone taps and location tracking (TF1 Info; Le Parisien). He said the national antiterrorism prosecutor's office is 'observing' the burning of the Limoges town hall and will decide within hours whether to take the case; about 5,000 people, 700 of them described by the authorities as 'radicalized and extremely violent,' had marched in Limoges (TF1 Info; not independently confirmed). Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said 557 people were held after the first day, 433 of them adults, and that most of those whose cases have been decided were little known to the police; she said she 'absolutely cannot confirm' that those arrested belong to the ultra-left, though black bloc groups were in the march from the start (TF1 Info; La Provence). A Paris police official, Michel Lavaud, said only 20 percent of those arrested in the Paris area since Saturday live in Paris (Le Parisien). Housing Minister Vincent Jeanbrun announced on X a circular with Darmanin to withhold from offenders' social benefits sums equal to the proceeds of looting or receiving stolen goods. Overseas, about 50 people were arrested after burning roadblocks and looting in Guadeloupe and Martinique (TF1 Info, from AFP). Coming days: Lecornu receives the unions on Wednesday morning and visits Limoges on Friday; a coordination of gilets jaunes has called an 'Act II' of protests for Saturday, 24 October, and Nuñez promised Marseille a larger police deployment that day; the CGT, which accuses the government of a 'strategy of chaos,' keeps its call for strikes and marches on 5 November (franceinfo; CNews; Le Parisien).

items.headline: Who is behind the riots: Lecornu points to an ultra-left network aiming at the election; Mediapart and LFI say intelligence officers were told to blame LFI
items.lead: Lecornu said on 19 October, citing the intelligence services, that an ultra-left movement wants to organize 'deep disorder' that could call into question the calendar of the presidential election; he met the heads of the DGSI and other intelligence services with Nuñez that evening (franceinfo; Le Parisien).
items.text: Lecornu said on 19 October, citing the intelligence services, that an ultra-left movement wants to organize 'deep disorder' that could call into question the calendar of the presidential election; he met the heads of the DGSI and other intelligence services with Nuñez that evening (franceinfo; Le Parisien). Mélenchon replied on X that as a candidate he had heard no one speak of this 'in private or in public,' and asked which group Lecornu meant. That evening he shared a Mediapart report, based on police sources, that a superior in the intelligence services told officers to write that La France insoumise was behind the movement; Mediapart's account has not been independently confirmed, and L'Opinion, citing a police source, reported the opposite view, that LFI helped plan the disorder. The facts so far do not settle the question: Paris prosecutor Beccuau said she cannot confirm that those arrested are from the ultra-left, and the DGSI denied a claim, made by a Journal du Dimanche journalist on CNews, that Kalashnikov rifles and submachine guns had been found on rioters (Le Parisien, citing BFMTV and Le Monde). On the far right, Éric Zemmour said on LCI on 18 October that the riots showed 'the true face of the great replacement,' describing 'a horde of North African and African barbarians'; LFI deputy Antoine Léaument has referred the remarks to the prosecutor. President Trump said in the United States that the unrest is 'linked to immigration, not to schools,' and the US Embassy advised Americans to avoid protest areas (TF1 Info, from AFP).

items.headline: Candidates compete on order: Bardella promises penal majority at 16, Glucksmann calls Mélenchon 'the stepping stone of the far right,' Attal wants social networks blocked
items.lead: The candidates spent 19 October setting out how they would restore order (the effect on voting intentions has not yet been measured by any poll taken after 17 October).
items.text: The candidates spent 19 October setting out how they would restore order (the effect on voting intentions has not yet been measured by any poll taken after 17 October). Jordan Bardella, at a National Rally press conference titled 'Facing chaos, the France of order,' called the weekend 'a political and security failure' and said that, if elected, the RN would lower the age of criminal majority to 16, suspend family allowances for families of repeat offenders, make looters pay for damage, set minimum sentences and give police more staff and equipment ('you touch a police officer, you sleep in prison'); he said neither he nor Marine Le Pen would attend Lecornu's meeting of party leaders, to which the RN will send a vice president (TF1 Info; CNews; RN). Raphaël Glucksmann, at the Paris town hall rally and on RTL, called for an 'extremely firm' response and said Mélenchon, by failing to condemn the violence clearly, is 'the stepping stone of the far right,' adding, 'Who will benefit from this chaos if not Mrs. Le Pen?' (France 24, from AFP; BFMTV; Le Parisien). Gabriel Attal (Renaissance) said 'the authority of the state has failed' and proposed temporarily blocking some social networks during exceptional events; Bruno Retailleau (LR) said a curfew is 'insufficient,' asked again for a state of emergency and proposed stripping dual nationals convicted of such violence of French citizenship; David Lisnard, mayor of Cannes and president of the mayors' association, said 'the state has become a fiction'; Marion Maréchal said Macron should consider resigning (TF1 Info). The mayors' association, which held rallies at town halls at noon, called the attacks 'premeditated' and asked for a change in police doctrine. Separately, the former prime minister François Fillon endorsed Retailleau on 17 October (La Dépêche).

items.headline: YouGov's first 2027 poll: Le Pen 35 to 37 percent, Mélenchon narrowly second; Polymarket eases to about 46 percent for Le Pen
items.lead: A YouGov poll for Le HuffPost, taken online from 12 to 15 October among 1,094 adults (976 registered voters) and published on 18 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 35 to 37 percent in the first round.
items.text: A YouGov poll for Le HuffPost, taken online from 12 to 15 October among 1,094 adults (976 registered voters) and published on 18 October, puts Marine Le Pen at 35 to 37 percent in the first round. Jean-Luc Mélenchon is second in every scenario with 13 to 16 percent, Raphaël Glucksmann has 12 to 14, and Édouard Philippe has 13 when he is the only centrist candidate and never more than 15; Gabriel Attal has 6 to 10, Bruno Retailleau 5 to 9, Marine Tondelier 5 to 6 and Fabien Roussel 3. In the second round Le Pen beats Philippe 52 to 48, Glucksmann, Attal and François Hollande 55 to 45 each, and Mélenchon 68 to 32 (Le HuffPost; second-round figures from the Commission des sondages notice as compiled by PollingForecast). The margin of error is 1.4 to 3.1 points. The fieldwork ended before the violence of 17 October. On Polymarket (about $154 million traded) Le Pen fell to about 46 percent early on 20 October from about 48 a day earlier; Philippe is at about 18.5, David Lisnard 11.75, Mélenchon 10.5 and Glucksmann 4.75.

items.headline: Budget: the Assembly suspends the vote on the revenue part and moves to the social security budget; minister says the debate has added €10 billion to the deficit
items.lead: The solemn vote on the first (revenue) part of the 2027 state budget, planned for Tuesday 20 October, has been postponed: the National Assembly stopped debating it at midnight on Monday with more than 2,600 amendments still to examine, and takes up the social security budget from Tuesday afternoon, as the constitutional deadlines require.
items.text: The solemn vote on the first (revenue) part of the 2027 state budget, planned for Tuesday 20 October, has been postponed: the National Assembly stopped debating it at midnight on Monday with more than 2,600 amendments still to examine, and takes up the social security budget from Tuesday afternoon, as the constitutional deadlines require. Debate on the state budget is due to resume on 27 October (LCP, from AFP; Capital, citing Le Monde and the Ministry for Relations with Parliament). Public Accounts Minister David Amiel said on Monday evening that the first week of debate had worsened the public deficit by €10 billion; deputies have rejected a key article on the tax allowance for pensions and much of a section on savings in local-government funding. The government's target is a deficit of 5 percent of GDP in 2027, against 5.4 percent in 2026. LCP expects the revenue part to be rejected in the end, which would send the bill to the Senate; Lecornu can still use Article 49.3, at the risk of a censure motion, or, from 18 December, budget ordinances, which have never been used.

items.headline: Three new runoff polls still show a technical tie; Polymarket slips to about 77 percent for Flávio
items.lead: Three national runoff polls were published on 19 October, six days before the 25 October vote.
items.text: Three national runoff polls were published on 19 October, six days before the 25 October vote. PoderData/Aya (3,000 telephone interviews, 16–18 October, margin of error 1.8 points, TSE registration BR-02586/2026) gives Flávio Bolsonaro 52 percent of valid votes and Lula 48, after a 50–50 tie in its previous round; in total votes it is 49 to 46. Rejection is 48 percent for Lula and 44 for Flávio, and Lula's disapproval rose to 50 percent from 47 (Exame; UOL). AtlasIntel/Bloomberg (4,998 online interviews, 13–18 October, margin of error 1 point, BR-02418/2026) gives Flávio 51.1 percent of valid votes and Lula 48.9, down from 52.8 to 47.2 on 9 October; in total votes it is 49.8 to 47.6 (UOL; Reuters via UOL). BTG/Nexus (2,002 telephone interviews, 16–18 October, margin of error 2 points, BR-04499/2026) has Flávio at 50.3 percent of valid votes and Lula at 49.7 (UOL; CNN Brasil). All three are within or close to the margin of error. On Polymarket (about $188 million traded) Flávio fell to about 77 percent early on 20 October from about 80 on 18 October, and Lula rose to about 21.5. Next: Quaest publishes a poll for Globo and O Globo on Wednesday 21 October (fieldwork 17–20 October, partly after the Band debate), Datafolha on Thursday 22 October, and both release final polls on Saturday 24 October (G1). Globo's runoff debate is on 23 October.

items.headline: Liberal MNAs sworn in, all to the people of Quebec; PQ cabinet to be sworn in on Wednesday without the lieutenant governor
items.lead: The 40 Liberal members of the National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room on 19 October; all of them took only the oath to the people of Quebec, not the optional oath to the King, and about half took it in both French and English (Canadian Press via L'actualité).
items.text: The 40 Liberal members of the National Assembly were sworn in at the Red Room on 19 October; all of them took only the oath to the people of Quebec, not the optional oath to the King, and about half took it in both French and English (Canadian Press via L'actualité). Liberal leader Charles Milliard presented his party as a 'government in waiting' and said it would be a reliable partner in solving crises but 'tough and intractable' on immigration to the regions, public finances and the national question; André Fortin is the Liberal house leader. One Liberal, Affine Lwalalika (Vachon), was not sworn in because of a judicial recount. Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon has written to Lieutenant Governor Manon Jeannotte asking her not to attend the swearing-in of his cabinet on Wednesday, 21 October; the oaths will be received by the secretary general of the government, and her office told Le Devoir that she will follow the ceremony on the Assembly's channel and sign the appointments at the same time (Le Devoir; the letter is reported by Le Devoir only and is not independently confirmed). The PQ has said it wants to abolish the lieutenant governor's post, which several experts consider very difficult under the Canadian Constitution.

items.headline: SpaceX reports third-quarter results today after the market closes; analysts expect revenue of about $12.7 billion
items.lead: SpaceX's third-quarter results had not been released by early 20 October; they are due after the New York market closes on Tuesday, with a webcast at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time (11:30 p.m. in Israel).
items.text: SpaceX's third-quarter results had not been released by early 20 October; they are due after the New York market closes on Tuesday, with a webcast at 4:30 p.m. Eastern time (11:30 p.m. in Israel). Analysts expect revenue of about $12.7 billion, against $7.8 billion in the second quarter, and earnings of 14 cents a share by LSEG's count (Reuters) or adjusted earnings of 15 cents and adjusted EBITDA of $6.59 billion by Bloomberg's (Yahoo Finance); in the second quarter SpaceX had a net loss of $541 million and AI capital spending of $15.8 billion (Reuters). Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas wrote on Monday that the need for more financing is 'a key overhang' and models debt issuance of $60 billion in 2027; CFO Bret Johnsen said last month that SpaceX would reach $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by year end (Yahoo Finance). Reuters reports growing talk of a SpaceX–Tesla merger: Barclays suggested last week that a deal could come before Tesla's annual meeting, which Tesla on Monday set for 3 December, with SpaceX the likelier buyer; neither company nor Musk has confirmed any plan. Tesla reports on Wednesday. SPCX closed on Monday at $147.96, up 1.3 percent from Friday's $146.03 (Yahoo Finance quote data).

items.headline: Musk pledges one of his SpaceX shares to every American child next year
items.lead: Elon Musk wrote on X on 19 October that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in the United States, adding, 'This will be the first of many'; he gave no details on eligibility or how the shares would be distributed.
items.text: Elon Musk wrote on X on 19 October that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in the United States, adding, 'This will be the first of many'; he gave no details on eligibility or how the shares would be distributed. At Friday's closing price and the Census Bureau's count of 72 million children under 18, the gift would be worth about $10.5 billion; Musk owns about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares, according to an August filing (CNBC). Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital, founder of Invest America, suggested the shares could go into the federal 'Trump accounts' for children. The post followed Anthropic's announcement that it plans to commit 5 percent of its shares to a public benefit fund; Musk replied that he recommends giving shares 'directly to the public.' CNBC noted that Musk did not follow through on some earlier pledges, such as up to $1 billion to OpenAI (he gave about $38 million) and $6 billion to the World Food Program. The Wall Street Journal and Forbes also reported the pledge.

items.headline: Grok Bot changelog adds version 0.71.2: tagged email addresses, prefilled forms, 250 MB attachments and up to 200 plugin skills
items.lead: The official Grok Bot changelog now lists version 0.71.2, dated 14 October, as the latest release; earlier editions of this digest found only version 0.70.2 of 11 October.
items.text: The official Grok Bot changelog now lists version 0.71.2, dated 14 October, as the latest release; earlier editions of this digest found only version 0.70.2 of 11 October. New: Bots can send from tagged forms of their email address (such as name+shop@) with routines that run only for that tag; forms a Bot asks you to fill can arrive with known fields filled in; team admins can stop members' Bots from messaging or handing work to other Bots; and a Bot whose computer runs low on disk names the largest files and deletes them only with your agreement. Improved: attachments of up to 250 MB and videos of up to 1 GB, up to 20 attachments per message instead of 6, up to 200 skills from installed plugins instead of 24, dropped voice calls that reconnect and continue, notifications on the computer in use rather than the phone, and batch actions on Outlook mail. The release also lists dozens of fixes, including longer connector time limits (two minutes instead of one) and fewer X rate-limit errors. This is the company's own changelog; the release date is the one it gives and could not be checked elsewhere. Cursor's changelog and SpaceXSI's news page show nothing new since the last edition.

items.headline: Land is the guest on a three-hour Cyphers interview about the CCRU, the Numogram and "Gnostic Calvinism"

items.text: The YouTube channel CYPHERS published a 3-hour-3-minute conversation with Nick Land on 17 October 2026, titled "Nick Land x Cyphers, CCRU, Numogram, Gnostic Calvinism, Accelerationism." items.headline: Land joins the online "Jesuit Cybernetic Culture Research Unit" (JCCRU) panel and answers its Christian critique of the CCRU
items.lead: Land spoke by video link on 9 October 2026 at the JCCRU panel, which the Methexis Institute held as part of Villanova University's Patristic, Medieval and Renaissance Conference.
items.text: The JCCRU is a panel organized by Ryan Haecker of the Methexis Institute, a research institute based in Austin, Texas. It was part of the 51st Patristic, Medieval and Renaissance (PMR) Conference at Villanova University, held 9 to 11 October 2026. The panel met online and streamed live on YouTube on Friday, 9 October, from 10:15 a.m. U.S. Eastern time (5:15 p.m. Israel time). Its stated aim is a Jesuit, Trinitarian critique of the original CCRU of the 1990s. Land joined remotely from Shanghai, late in the session after technical trouble with a new computer. He spoke about a return of theological debates, including the debate between Reformed and Roman Catholic Christianity, in a culture shaped by cybernetics and AI. He said the Bible cannot be read literally, said his own access to the tradition is "neo-Pythagorean" and numerical, and described his intellectual path since the CCRU as "retrochronic" rediscovery rather than a change of views. Other speakers included Aaron Khokhar, Darius Branche, Ashton Arnoldy and John Esposito. The full stream and an edited 13-minute clip of Land's response are on YouTube; Haecker announced Land's participation on X on 9 October.

items.headline: Land says the Trinity diagram, the Seal of Solomon and the Yijing are 'crayon sketches' of the Numogram
items.lead: On 17 October Land posted that the 'standard diagram of the Christian Trinity, the Seal of Solomon, and the Yijing are all crayon sketches of the Numogram Time Zones, confirmed.'
items.text: On 17 October Land posted that the 'standard diagram of the Christian Trinity, the Seal of Solomon, and the Yijing are all crayon sketches of the Numogram Time Zones, confirmed.' He was quoting a thread by Ryan Haecker, the JCCRU organizer, which argued that for Land artificial intelligence is 'the anti-Trinity.' Land replied to Haecker that if there is a choice, he will 'never' side against the Numogram: 'Exoteric familial metaphor versus Decimal Revelation is a no-brainer.' The post had about 15,000 views. This continues the exchange that began at the 9 October JCCRU panel.

items.headline: 'Gnostic Calvinism' is Land's most frequent theme on X since late August
items.lead: Since 23 August Land has used the phrase 'Gnostic Calvinism' in more than a dozen X posts, mostly short and often ironic, without yet publishing a full statement of what it means.
items.text: Since 23 August Land has used the phrase 'Gnostic Calvinism' in more than a dozen X posts, mostly short and often ironic, without yet publishing a full statement of what it means. items.headline: KJV and gematria: Land answers Bronze Age Pervert, and a listener identifies the KJV numerics writer he mentioned on Cyphers
items.lead: On 31 August, replying to Bronze Age Pervert's 'God doesn't exist,' Land wrote: 'The God that doesn't exist is a misinterpretation of the King James Bible.'
items.text: On 31 August, replying to Bronze Age Pervert's 'God doesn't exist,' Land wrote: 'The God that doesn't exist is a misinterpretation of the King James Bible.' items.headline: JCCRU speaker Ashton K. Arnoldy posts the talk and the exchange with Land on Christ
items.lead: Ashton K. Arnoldy, one of the 9 October JCCRU panelists, posted the talk "Beauty Will Not Be Updated: Anagoge beyond the Cybercosm" and the exchange with Land that followed it about the metaphysical status of Christ.
items.text: The 20-minute video, "Aesthetic combat & Nick Land on the reality of Christ," went up on the micr0k0sm YouTube channel late on 19 October; the description puts Land's part on Christ at 12:43. A companion essay on Substack under Arnoldy's name followed shortly after midnight Israel time. Ryan Haecker of the Methexis Institute, who organized the panel, shared the essay on X on 20 October. The talk asks whether AI can persuade people that "technology eating the universe is beautiful," or whether beauty discloses something that "cannot be updated."

items.headline: Four Tuesday polls: Walla has Eisenkot's Yashar ahead of Likud 23 to 19, Channel 14 has Likud far ahead and the coalition at 62
items.lead: Four polls published on Tuesday, 20 October, a week before the 27 October vote, again split by outlet.
items.text: Four polls published on Tuesday, 20 October, a week before the 27 October vote, again split by outlet. Walla (Lazar Research with Panel4All; 601 people questioned on 19 October; margin of error 4 points): Yashar 23 seats, Likud 19, Beyachad 14, the Democrats 9, Yisrael Beytenu 8, Shas 8, Otzma Yehudit 8, the Joint List 8, United Torah Judaism 7, Religious Zionism–Zehut 6, Ra'am 6 and the Reservists 4; Winter's party is at 2.9 percent, below the threshold. Blocs: Netanyahu's coalition 48, the opposition 54, the Arab parties 14 (Jerusalem Post; JFeed). Channel 14 (poll by Shlomo Filber): Likud 30, Yashar 20, Beyachad 9; coalition 62, opposition 44, Arab parties 14; in a direct contest Netanyahu leads Eisenkot 56 to 44 (Skarim poll archive; Globes/ice.co.il). The poll aggregator israelielections.com also lists i24News/Direct Polls (Likud 26, Yashar 20, Beyachad 12) and Maagar Mochot for 103FM (Yashar 21, Likud 18, Beyachad 15, with the Reservists and Amcha at 4 each); for these two the aggregator is the only source found, so the figures are unconfirmed. Polymarket's 'next prime minister' market has Eisenkot at about 50 percent, Netanyahu at 27.5 and Bennett at 12.5 (about $49.7 million traded).

items.headline: Netanyahu and Smotrich press Winter's rabbi to get him to quit; Winter refuses, and Hanegbi says he will vote for Liberman
items.lead: Netanyahu and Bezalel Smotrich met Rabbi Eli Sadan, the mentor of candidate Winter, on Tuesday to press Winter to withdraw so his votes are not lost below the threshold; Winter refused, saying 'we are going all the way' (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post).
items.text: Netanyahu and Bezalel Smotrich met Rabbi Eli Sadan, the mentor of candidate Winter, on Tuesday to press Winter to withdraw so his votes are not lost below the threshold; Winter refused, saying 'we are going all the way' (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post). Nissim Louk, the father of Shani Louk, who was murdered on 7 October 2023, endorsed Winter. Channel 12 reported, via the Times of Israel, that Netanyahu also phoned Moti Leitner of the Charedi Public party on Saturday; Leitner is staying in the race. Separately, Tzachi Hanegbi, a longtime Likud politician and Netanyahu's former national security adviser, wrote in Ynet that he will vote for Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu, citing the 'messianic right,' the 'racist right' and the exemption of Haredim from the draft (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post; Arutz Sheva). Ben Gvir said on the evening of 18 October that Netanyahu's office had promised European countries to keep Otzma Yehudit out of the next government; he gave no proof, and Likud called the claim 'false political spin.' Hours earlier Netanyahu had answered 'Absolutely' when asked whether Otzma would be in his government (Arutz Sheva; Ynetnews).

items.headline: 42 Chabad men detained at Ben Gurion over draft evasion; Netanyahu condemns the arrests; election committee fines Likud over IDF footage
items.lead: Military police detained 42 Chabad men at Ben Gurion Airport on 20 October on draft-evasion charges; most were released after agreeing to enlist, and Ynet reports two were kept in custody (Ynetnews; Jerusalem Post).
items.text: Military police detained 42 Chabad men at Ben Gurion Airport on 20 October on draft-evasion charges; most were released after agreeing to enlist, and Ynet reports two were kept in custody (Ynetnews; Jerusalem Post). Netanyahu called the arrests a 'deliberate attempt to harm the process of drafting Haredim without coercion,' and Haredi protesters blocked a highway (Times of Israel). The IDF has asked the Justice Ministry and the Central Elections Committee to cancel Netanyahu's planned speech at Wednesday's officer-cadet graduation, on the grounds that it would be electioneering (Channel 13 and Haaretz, via the Times of Israel). The chairman of the Central Elections Committee, Justice Sohlberg, ruled that Likud's campaign ads illegally used IDF Spokesperson footage; Likud must pay NIS 1,500 to the petitioner and NIS 6,000 to the state, and any further use needs advance approval and payment (Haaretz, headline and summary only because of the paywall; JFeed).

items.headline: Tampa talks end their first day without agreement; Israel wants a joint operations room to verify pilot zones, Lebanon objects
items.lead: The Lebanese and Israeli military delegations met for about six hours at US Central Command in Tampa on 20 October without reaching agreement, and resume on Wednesday, 21 October (Anadolu; Annahar).
items.text: The Lebanese and Israeli military delegations met for about six hours at US Central Command in Tampa on 20 October without reaching agreement, and resume on Wednesday, 21 October (Anadolu; Annahar). Lebanon sent three officers instead of the six first planned. According to Annahar and Anadolu, it asked for an end to demolitions and firing, an organized Israeli withdrawal, new 'model' areas cleared of weapons, the release of prisoners, the return of residents and access for the olive harvest. Israel wants a direct operations room with the Lebanese army to verify that the pilot zones are clear, which Lebanon rejects. The villages discussed for the pilot are Froun, Sarifa and Zawtar al-Sharqiya, possibly extended to near Tallat Ali Taher. A US official told the Times of Israel the meeting is at working level, without the two ambassadors.

items.headline: Military court summons two Hezbollah officials over a seized explosives shipment
items.lead: Claude Ghanem, the government commissioner to Lebanon's military court, on 20 October summoned two Hezbollah officials known as 'Sajed' and 'Dulfiqar' over the explosives shipment that army intelligence seized at Dahr al-Baidar, and security agencies are trying to locate them (MTV; Naharnet; Times of Israel).
items.text: Claude Ghanem, the government commissioner to Lebanon's military court, on 20 October summoned two Hezbollah officials known as 'Sajed' and 'Dulfiqar' over the explosives shipment that army intelligence seized at Dahr al-Baidar, and security agencies are trying to locate them (MTV; Naharnet; Times of Israel). Naharnet, citing AFP, dates the seizure to 8 October and puts the load at half a ton; MTV says 780 kilograms (an earlier item on this page gave a different date). It is one of three large explosives shipments seized this month, and US Secretary of State Rubio has urged Lebanon not to hand the explosives back.

items.headline: First poll after the riots: Ifop has Le Pen at 34 to 38 percent, Mélenchon second and Philippe out in every scenario
items.lead: An Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, taken online from the evening of 17 October to 19 October among 1,928 registered voters and published on 20 October, is the first measured after the 17 October violence.
items.text: An Ifop-Fiducial poll for LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, taken online from the evening of 17 October to 19 October among 1,928 registered voters and published on 20 October, is the first measured after the 17 October violence. First round: Le Pen 34 to 38 percent, Mélenchon 15 to 20, Glucksmann 12 to 16 and Philippe 12 to 16, and Philippe fails to reach the runoff in every scenario. In the main scenario, with Philippe as the only centrist: Le Pen 36, Mélenchon 16.5, Philippe 15, Glucksmann 14, Retailleau 7.5. Second round: Le Pen beats Mélenchon 68 to 32, Glucksmann 57 to 43, Hollande 59 to 41, Attal 58 to 42 and Philippe 56 to 44; in Ifop's previous wave (12–14 October) the Le Pen–Philippe runoff was 52 to 48. Polymarket barely moved: Le Pen about 46.5 percent, Philippe 18.5, Lisnard 11.7, Mélenchon 10.5, Glucksmann 5.

items.headline: Soldiers to guard sites so police are free for Saturday; curfews spread to Marseille and Bordeaux; 700 brought before judges
items.lead: Prime Minister Lecornu promised a 'massive' security operation for Saturday, 24 October, when student unions and the gilets jaunes plan new protests, and Interior Minister Nuñez told parliament that Operation Sentinelle soldiers will take over static guard duties to free police officers; he is also considering a ban on undeclared demonstrations (Euronews; France 24).
items.text: Prime Minister Lecornu promised a 'massive' security operation for Saturday, 24 October, when student unions and the gilets jaunes plan new protests, and Interior Minister Nuñez told parliament that Operation Sentinelle soldiers will take over static guard duties to free police officers; he is also considering a ban on undeclared demonstrations (Euronews; France 24). Monday night passed without notable incidents. On Tuesday night curfews were renewed in about a dozen towns (central Lyon; Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain for minors; Nice for minors until 25 October), and new ones began in Marseille (minors, 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. until Friday, 23 October, also covering Aubagne, Cabriès and Les Pennes-Mirabeau) and in Bordeaux (minors, until 26 October). In Paris the curfew around République and Les Halles runs from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., and undeclared gatherings are banned from 8 p.m. (BFMTV). Justice Ministry spokesman Sacha Straub-Khan said that of about 2,500 people held in custody, 700 have been brought before a magistrate, about 20 percent of cases have been dropped, and more than 70 judicial investigations are open (franceinfo); a franceinfo video headline gives 149 people jailed, a figure found in no second source.

items.headline: Real Time Big Data has Flávio ahead 48 to 45; Polymarket rises back to about 81 percent; Quaest and Datafolha due Wednesday and Thursday
items.lead: A Real Time Big Data poll published on 20 October (2,000 voters, 15–19 October, margin of error 2 points, registered with the electoral court as BR-02952/2026) puts Flávio Bolsonaro at 48 percent and Lula at 45, or 52 to 48 in valid votes (Brasil de Fato).
items.text: A Real Time Big Data poll published on 20 October (2,000 voters, 15–19 October, margin of error 2 points, registered with the electoral court as BR-02952/2026) puts Flávio Bolsonaro at 48 percent and Lula at 45, or 52 to 48 in valid votes (Brasil de Fato). Quaest publishes its next runoff poll on Wednesday morning (2,154 interviews, 17–20 October) and Datafolha on Thursday afternoon; both plan final polls on Saturday, 24 October, the day before the vote. On Polymarket, Flávio has risen to about 81 percent from about 77 in the last edition, with Lula at about 19.5 percent (about $190 million traded).

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon's cabinet is sworn in today: about 20 ministers, a minister for the independence process, and Paradis as chief negotiator
items.lead: The Parti Québécois cabinet is sworn in on Wednesday, 21 October, at 1:30 p.m. Quebec time (8:30 p.m. Israel time), without the lieutenant governor, Manon Jeannotte, who was not invited and will sign the appointment acts in her office (Le Devoir; Radio-Canada).
items.text: The Parti Québécois cabinet is sworn in on Wednesday, 21 October, at 1:30 p.m. Quebec time (8:30 p.m. Israel time), without the lieutenant governor, Manon Jeannotte, who was not invited and will sign the appointment acts in her office (Le Devoir; Radio-Canada). The cabinet is a reduced one of about 20 ministers, against 28 under Fréchette, and includes a 'minister responsible for the independence process'; Pascal Paradis is named Quebec's chief negotiator. The government's 100-day priorities are a special budget for homelessness, a lower gas tax, a secretariat for government efficiency and regulatory relief, and lower immigration levels. PQ members meet former premier Pauline Marois and Jean Royer on Thursday, and the National Assembly session opens in late November.

items.headline: EU adopts its Arctic strategy: a direct cable from Greenland to Europe, €200 million for Greenland, and shared icebreakers
items.lead: The European Commission and High Representative Kaja Kallas adopted 'Europe's Northern Neighbourhood – A New Strategy for the Arctic' on 20 October, with four priorities: security and resilience, climate, prosperity, and people (European Commission; EEAS).
items.text: The European Commission and High Representative Kaja Kallas adopted 'Europe's Northern Neighbourhood – A New Strategy for the Arctic' on 20 October, with four priorities: security and resilience, climate, prosperity, and people (European Commission; EEAS). Its measures include an Arctic Cable Hub, possibly a first step toward a maritime security hub; wider Copernicus and Galileo satellite coverage; joint purchase and pooling of icebreakers; military mobility; €260 million from the European Defence Fund; a Pan-Arctic Cable that links Greenland directly to Europe; Arctic coverage for the IRIS² satellite network; €200 million for Greenland; and the Rail Nordica project. Asked why there is no new budget, Kallas named the satellite upgrades as the concrete step within 12 months and said the EU is open to working with the United States 'if they so wish.' Greenland's broadcaster KNR notes that the EU has already put €107 million into the Greenland cable, and Commission President von der Leyen presented the strategy as a response to Russia. Greenland's reaction was not found in a second source.

items.headline: SpaceX's third quarter: revenue up 161 percent to $14.6 billion and a $4.4 billion profit, driven by AI; Cursor added $608 million
items.lead: SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.575 billion on 20 October, up 161 percent from $5.576 billion a year earlier and from $7.814 billion in the second quarter, well above the LSEG analyst estimate of $12.72 billion (SEC filing; Reuters).
items.text: SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.575 billion on 20 October, up 161 percent from $5.576 billion a year earlier and from $7.814 billion in the second quarter, well above the LSEG analyst estimate of $12.72 billion (SEC filing; Reuters). Net income was $4.404 billion, against a loss of $1.054 billion a year earlier; operating income was $2.791 billion and adjusted EBITDA $8.809 billion. Diluted GAAP earnings were 35 cents a share; Reuters, using adjusted figures, reports 45 cents against an expected 13 cents. By segment: AI (the 'SI' segment, which includes xAI and Cursor) brought in $7.560 billion, up 195 percent from the second quarter and 830 percent from a year earlier, with operating income of $431 million after $1.2 billion of share-based pay tied to the Cursor purchase; Connectivity (Starlink) $5.248 billion; Space $1.767 billion. Capital spending was $19.593 billion, of which $16.444 billion went to AI. Starlink has 13.6 million consumer subscribers paying an average of $69 a month, and the company has 1.7 gigawatts of nameplate computing capacity as Colossus II is built. The Cursor deal closed on 14 August at an implied equity value of $60 billion (GAAP consideration $42.5 billion), and Cursor contributed $608 million of revenue through 30 September. The release also names Starship Flight 14 as the first revenue-earning orbital flight (26 Starlink V3 satellites), a planned Starbase in Louisiana with a first launch targeted for 2029, and an 800 MHz spectrum deal signed on 8 October, and it mentions Grok Bot. Yahoo Finance reports a backlog of $63 billion, $42 billion of it expected within a year.

items.headline: Musk: SpaceX and Tesla have set up independent committees to study a merger; shares rise after hours
items.lead: On the earnings call Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed a special committee of independent directors to explore a merger; he called it 'a good idea' but said it is not certain, no terms are agreed, and a deal would need a majority of all outstanding Tesla shares, describing the process as 'an odd kabuki dance' (Yahoo Finance; BBC; Reuters).
items.text: On the earnings call Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have each formed a special committee of independent directors to explore a merger; he called it 'a good idea' but said it is not certain, no terms are agreed, and a deal would need a majority of all outstanding Tesla shares, describing the process as 'an odd kabuki dance' (Yahoo Finance; BBC; Reuters). Musk also said he expects $500 billion to $1 trillion of annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 (Reuters), and that the Terafab chip plant should produce a test chip in about May or June 2027, with volume production in the third quarter of 2028. SpaceX shares (SPCX) rose about 8 percent after hours by Reuters' count (Bloomberg reported 4.6 percent), and Tesla about 2 percent; Tesla reports its own results on Wednesday, 21 October.

items.headline: City breaks ground on the restoration of the Carver Center, the 1922 hall where Ella Fitzgerald and Duke Ellington played
items.lead: The City of Trenton broke ground on 20 October on the first phase of restoring the Carver Center at 40 Fowler Street: a contract of about $2.53 million for the roof and exterior, part of a restoration expected to cost about $8 million (Trenton Journal, from a city release; InsiderNJ).
items.text: The City of Trenton broke ground on 20 October on the first phase of restoring the Carver Center at 40 Fowler Street: a contract of about $2.53 million for the roof and exterior, part of a restoration expected to cost about $8 million (Trenton Journal, from a city release; InsiderNJ). The building was put up in 1922 by the Sunlight Elks Lodge and renamed for George Washington Carver by the YMCA in 1944; Ella Fitzgerald, Count Basie and Duke Ellington performed there. The city bought it in 2021. Government role: this is a public project, and the first phase is paid for with federal Community Development Block Grant money.

items.headline: The JCCRU debate continues in writing: Y-3 answers Haecker with 'The Cybernetic Aggiornamento'
items.lead: The Substack writer Y-3 (@RvelinEdu) published 'The Cybernetic Aggiornamento' on 20 October (U.S. time), his reply to Ryan Haecker's 16 October essay 'Breaking the Cybernetic Silence,' which in turn answered Y-3's 10 October essay 'Nick Land, Ryan Haecker, and the Problem of Cybernetic Consciousness.'
items.text: The Substack writer Y-3 (@RvelinEdu) published 'The Cybernetic Aggiornamento' on 20 October (U.S. time), his reply to Ryan Haecker's 16 October essay 'Breaking the Cybernetic Silence,' which in turn answered Y-3's 10 October essay 'Nick Land, Ryan Haecker, and the Problem of Cybernetic Consciousness.' Y-3 argues that Haecker's project of joining Jesuit theology to CCRU cybernetics is a technological version of the Catholic 'aggiornamento' (updating) of the Second Vatican Council, names the Jesuit Pierre Teilhard de Chardin as its closest precursor, and warns, citing Kierkegaard and E. L. Mascall, that an attempt to make modernity Christian can end by making Christianity modern. Haecker quoted the essay on X. Separately, on 14 October the writer Alex Mazey posted an essay titled 'AQ & Nick Land: Psychotic Schizo-LARP or the Retroactive Diagnosis of Outsideness?', which he says appeared in ŠUM Journal, and @resonatingloop of the Cyphers circle shared it; the essay itself could not be found online, so its contents are not confirmed.

items.headline: Two Wednesday polls: Yashar leads Likud in both; Winter's party is in on Channel 12 and out on Channel 13
items.lead: Channel 12 and Channel 13 published polls on Wednesday, 21 October, six days before the 27 October vote, and both put Eisenkot's Yashar first.
items.text: Channel 12 and Channel 13 published polls on Wednesday, 21 October, six days before the 27 October vote, and both put Eisenkot's Yashar first. Channel 13 (Midgam Project, Camil Fuchs): Yashar 20 seats, Likud 19, Beyachad 14, the Democrats 10, the Joint List 9, United Torah Judaism 8, Yisrael Beytenu 8, Religious Zionism–Zehut 8, Otzma Yehudit 7, Shas 7, Ra'am 6 and the Reservists (Hendel and Zelekha) 4; Ofer Winter's party falls below the threshold. Blocs: opposition 52, Netanyahu's coalition 49, Arab parties 15 (Skarim poll archive; israelielections.com). Channel 12 (Midgam, Mano Geva; 505 people): Yashar 23, Likud 19, Beyachad 15, the Democrats 9, the Joint List 9, Shas 8, Yisrael Beytenu 8, Otzma Yehudit 7, United Torah Judaism 7, Religious Zionism–Zehut 6, Ra'am 5 and Winter's Amcha Yisrael 4, with the Reservists below the threshold. These Channel 12 seat figures come from the israelielections.com aggregator only and are unconfirmed; Haaretz and Maariv headlines confirm that Winter passes and Hendel–Zelekha fail in the Channel 12 poll, and the reverse in the Channel 13 poll.

items.headline: Winter and Leitner refuse to quit despite a Smotrich offer of a ministry; Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, even in a rotation
items.lead: Bezalel Smotrich offered on 21 October to give up one of his party's ministerial posts to Ofer Winter if Winter withdrew; Winter refused.
items.text: Bezalel Smotrich offered on 21 October to give up one of his party's ministerial posts to Ofer Winter if Winter withdrew from the race; Winter refused, saying 'we didn't come for jobs' and 'we are in the right-wing camp, but there will be no blank check' (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post; Ynet). Earlier in the day Winter said it may have been a mistake to pledge early that he would recommend only Netanyahu, then said he stands by it. Moti Leitner of the Charedi Public party also said he would stay in after meeting Netanyahu, though Likud officials told Walla and Kan they still expect him to drop out. Gadi Eisenkot pledged on air that he will not sit in a government led by Netanyahu, not even under a rotation deal, and that he would resign within an hour if he did (Haaretz; Times of Israel; Davar). Separately, minister May Golan (Likud) was questioned for about 11 hours by the Lahav 433 police unit in a bribery case (Haaretz; Ynet).

items.headline: Netanyahu says Iran is trying again to build a bomb and that he has ordered the IDF and Mossad to topple the regime; soldiers begin voting
items.lead: Speaking at the officer-cadet graduation on 21 October, Netanyahu said Iran is 'again trying to develop the bombs of death' and that he has instructed the IDF and the Mossad to bring down the regime.
items.text: Speaking at the officer-cadet graduation on 21 October, Netanyahu said Iran is 'again trying to develop the bombs of death' and that he has instructed the IDF and the Mossad to bring down the regime; Defense Minister Katz said that if Iran attacks Israel, 'Iran will burn' (Times of Israel, Ynet and Kan, as listed by israelielections.com). A security source told Globes it was not aware of the information Netanyahu cited. The attorney general barred a live broadcast of the speech as election propaganda, and the IDF did not stream any part of the ceremony. Also on Wednesday, soldiers began voting at more than 850 polling stations at bases and outposts, including in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria (All Israel News; Maariv), and the Central Bureau of Statistics said 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, about 810,000 of whom live abroad (Times of Israel; Kan). The Bank of Israel held its rate at 3.25 percent.

items.headline: Tampa military talks end after two days without agreement; Macron will hold a conference for the Lebanese army after the Israeli vote
items.lead: The second day of US-mediated talks between the Lebanese and Israeli military delegations at Central Command in Tampa ended on 21 October without agreement.
items.text: The second day of US-mediated talks between the Lebanese and Israeli military delegations at Central Command in Tampa ended on 21 October without agreement or any expansion of the pilot zones (MTV; Jarayid, from Lebanese media). The dispute is still who verifies what happens in the south: Israel wants a direct joint operations room with the Lebanese army, and Lebanon refuses any arrangement that gives Israel a say over its army's movements and wants contact to go through the United States. Lebanese reports say the third day is set aside for the US side to review the results, with possible separate meetings with each delegation. In Doha, President Macron said France will organize a conference to support the Lebanese army 'in the coming weeks,' but only after the Israeli election, since holding it before would be 'useless'; he called the pressure on Lebanon 'the least best way' to deal with Hezbollah and said disarmament needs an Israeli withdrawal with confidence-building measures (Naharnet, from AFP; Times of Israel).

items.headline: Quaest: Flávio 45, Lula 44, still a technical tie; Lula's rejection falls to 47 percent; Datafolha due Thursday
items.lead: A Quaest poll for Globo published on 21 October has Flávio Bolsonaro at 45 percent and Lula at 44 in the runoff, a technical tie.
items.text: A Quaest poll for Globo and O Globo published on 21 October (2,154 voters in 124 cities, 17–20 October, margin of error 2 points, registered as BR-08535/2026) has Flávio Bolsonaro at 45 percent and Lula at 44 in the 25 October runoff, against 46 to 44 a week earlier; blank, null or not voting 9 percent, undecided 2. In valid votes that is about 50.6 to 49.4, by UOL's calculation. In the unprompted question both have 40 percent. Rejection moved toward Lula: 52 percent say they would never vote for Flávio (54 before) and 47 percent for Lula (53 before). Approval of the Lula government rose to 46 percent, with 47 percent disapproving (g1; UOL). It is Quaest's first poll since the end of the 6x1 work schedule, a Lula campaign promise, was enacted. Datafolha publishes on Thursday, 22 October. Polymarket has Flávio at about 79 percent, Lula about 21.

items.headline: Unions leave Matignon empty-handed and call a general strike for 5 November; Lecornu meets the parties on Thursday
items.lead: The five main unions met Prime Minister Lecornu for two and a half hours on 21 October and came out saying he announced no measures.
items.text: The five main unions met Prime Minister Lecornu for two and a half hours on 21 October and came out saying he announced no measures; CGT leader Sophie Binet called for strike meetings everywhere and said 'the strike must take over' from 5 November, the date nearly all unions have set for a general strike in the private and public sectors (Nouvel Obs, from AFP; RTS; L'Humanité). The CFTC said the government had opened the door to talks on the minimum wage, and Lecornu has promised first announcements for young people early next week. On Thursday, 22 October, he receives the political parties on the 17 October violence and on securing the presidential campaign, and Macron holds a meeting with the intelligence services on the failures of that day. Curfews were renewed on Wednesday night in parts of Paris, Lille, Lyon and Marseille, and undeclared gatherings remain banned in Paris ahead of Saturday's protests (franceinfo; RFI). Polymarket is unchanged, with Le Pen at about 46.5 percent.

items.headline: Macron calls foreign leaders' comments on the riots 'stupid' and says AI-made videos are being used in their campaigns
items.lead: Speaking in Doha on 21 October, Macron rejected what he called 'stupid' comments by foreign leaders who blamed the French riots on Muslim migrants.
items.text: Speaking in Doha on 21 October, Macron rejected what he called 'stupid' comments by foreign leaders who blamed the French riots on Muslim migrants, and said fake videos made with artificial intelligence were being used for their own political campaigns (AP; The Guardian; BBC). He named no one, but the reports tie the remarks to Trump, who had said France should 'close your borders,' and to Netanyahu's comments on i24NEWS; Mélenchon separately accused Netanyahu of meddling in French politics (Ynet). At home, Macron called for firmness against those responsible for the violence but made no announcement on wages, purchasing power or public services.

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon's cabinet is sworn in: 22 ministers, with Gentilcore as deputy premier and minister for Quebec's accession to independence
items.lead: Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon and 22 ministers were sworn in at the National Assembly on 21 October.
items.text: Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon and 22 ministers were sworn in at the National Assembly on 21 October (TVA Nouvelles, from QMI; Journal de Montréal; Radio-Canada). St-Pierre Plamondon also keeps the fight against homelessness. Catherine Gentilcore is deputy premier, minister of immigration and integration, minister responsible for Quebec's accession to independence, and government house leader. Nicolas Marceau has finance and infrastructure; Alain Therrien is president of the Treasury Board; Marie-Karlynn Laflamme has health; Joël Arseneau has education; Marie-Claude Sarrazin has justice and Canadian intergovernmental affairs, plus relations with English-speaking Quebecers and secularism; Pascal Bérubé has culture and the French language; Guy Jr Lapointe has a new 'internal security' ministry; Dieudonné Ella Oyono has international relations and foreign trade; and Anne Nguyen is junior minister for artificial intelligence and digital affairs.

items.headline: Locust Hill Cemetery, Trenton's 1861 Black burial ground, becomes a site on the New Jersey Black Heritage Trail
items.lead: The New Jersey Historical Commission marked Locust Hill Cemetery in Trenton as a site on the state's Black Heritage Trail at a ceremony on 20 October.
items.text: The New Jersey Historical Commission marked Locust Hill Cemetery in Trenton as a site on the state's Black Heritage Trail at a ceremony on 20 October (NBC10 Philadelphia; PIX11). Mount Zion AME Church bought the land in 1861 as a burial ground for Black residents; 174 people are known to be buried there, including at least 10 Civil War veterans. The late Algernon Ward nominated the site, it was approved in 2024, and City Council approved the marker on 16 December 2025. The trail was set up in 2022. No reusable photo was found; NBC10's report has photos of the ceremony.

items.headline: Trump says he is open to a three-way meeting with Xi and Putin in China next month, with nuclear weapons on the agenda
items.lead: Trump told reporters on 19 October that he would hold a three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during his November visit to China 'if President Xi wants to have it.'
items.text: Trump told reporters on 19 October, Washington time, that he would hold a three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during his November visit to China 'if President Xi wants to have it,' to talk about 'nuclear weapons and denuclearisation' (South China Morning Post; Caixin). Caixin reports he said he had only just heard of the proposal and understood the meeting would take place in China, around the APEC summit in Shenzhen; Kremlin spokesman Peskov had said such talks would be useful. No date, format or agenda has been agreed, and China has not confirmed it.

items.headline: Tesla's third quarter: profit down 29 percent to $787 million, while the merger study with SpaceX goes on
items.lead: Tesla reported third-quarter revenue of $28.05 billion and net income of $787 million on 21 October, a profit 29 percent lower than a year earlier.
items.text: Tesla reported third-quarter revenue of $28.05 billion and net income of $787 million on 21 October, a profit 29 percent lower than a year earlier; adjusted earnings were 48 cents a share, above forecasts. Automotive revenue fell 3 percent to $20.56 billion, services revenue rose 33 percent to $4.61 billion, and free cash flow was $1.53 billion (CNBC; AP). The results come a day after Musk said both companies had set up committees of independent directors to study a merger; AP says no terms have been agreed. The detailed figures are from CNBC; AP confirms the drop in profit.

items.headline: Grok Bot: SpaceX gives a first user count of 800,000 paying weekly users, and the company says Bot can now build reports, memos and dashboards
items.lead: On SpaceX's earnings call on 20 October, president Gwynne Shotwell said Grok Bot had 800,000 paid weekly users earlier this month, more than double a month before.
items.text: On SpaceX's earnings call on 20 October, president Gwynne Shotwell said Grok Bot had 800,000 paid weekly users earlier this month, more than double a month before, and called business customers the fastest-growing group; Musk said wide deployment for companies should come 'within a few weeks' (TSN, from the call transcript). The company did not define a paid weekly user, and the number is not in the written filing. On 21 October the official @bot account on X said 'Grok Bot can now build reports, memos, and dashboards' that users can edit with it or have it keep up to date, without further details on plans or availability (TSN). A secondary report says a 'What's new' video posted on 20 October by Matt Palmer, who works on the product, shows Bot reading and answering X Chat messages and being set as the default assistant on Android phones (HIMIAO, citing Tesla North); that report is unconfirmed. The official changelog is still at version 0.71.2 of 14 October.
