items.headline: Final polls before Tuesday's vote: Yashar 23, Likud 21 in both Israel Hayom and the Times of Israel; neither bloc near 61
items.lead: The final polls before the 27 October vote put Eisenkot's Yashar first in both.
items.text: The final polls before the 27 October vote put Eisenkot's Yashar first in both. Israel Hayom's final Kantar poll (21–22 October, 1,110 respondents, margin of error 3 points): Yashar 23 seats, Likud 21, Bennett's B'Yachad 14 (up), Yisrael Beytenu 7 (down) and the Reservists (Hendel and Zelekha) 4, with Winter's party below the threshold; the Netanyahu bloc has 50 seats. The final Times of Israel/Zman Yisrael poll, published on 22 October, has the same top two: Yashar 23 (three fewer than a week earlier), Likud 21, B'Yachad 11, Yisrael Beytenu 9, the Joint List 9, Shas, United Torah Judaism, the Democrats and Otzma Yehudit 8 each, Religious Zionism 6, Ra'am 5 and the Reservists 4; each Jewish-led bloc gets 51. Its fieldwork dates are given as 14–15 October (500 respondents, margin of error 4.4 points), which is earlier than its publication suggests. In that poll almost 60 percent said Netanyahu should leave politics if he fails to form a government, against 29 percent, and 87 percent said their vote is final. The Israel Hayom figures are confirmed by the Israel 2026 poll tracker and JFeed.

items.headline: High Court bars parties from collecting real-time turnout data at polling stations; Shin Bet removes 'foreign influence' accounts
items.lead: On 22 October the High Court ruled, 2 to 1, that party-appointed polling-station members and observers may not count voters with digital tools and send running turnout figures to their parties on election day.
items.text: On 22 October the High Court ruled, 2 to 1, that party-appointed polling-station members and observers may not count voters with digital tools and send running turnout figures to their parties on election day. Justices Khaled Kabub and Ruth Ronnen formed the majority and Justice David Mintz dissented; the ruling overturns permission given by the acting director of the Central Elections Committee (Times of Israel; Jerusalem Post; Ynet). Parties use such figures to direct get-out-the-vote work on the day. The same day the Shin Bet said it had worked with the State Attorney's cyber department and the elections committee to remove a number of social media profiles that were part of a 'foreign influence campaign'; it did not say how many or which country was behind them (Times of Israel). Netanyahu, interviewed by Arutz Sheva, framed the vote as 'me and Trump or Eisenkot and Abbas.'

items.text: The US-mediated military talks between Israel and Lebanon at Central Command in Tampa closed on 22 October, after a third day, without agreement and without a date for a next round (Ynet; The New Arab). The gap is the one reported earlier: Israel wants a role in verifying Hezbollah's disarmament in the south, and Lebanon wants an independent international mechanism instead. No new Israeli reaction to the EU security mission in Lebanon (EUSM Lebanon) and no new contributing countries were found.

items.headline: Datafolha three days before the runoff: Flávio 47, Lula 46, a 50–50 tie in valid votes; Lula's approval edges ahead
items.lead: Datafolha's runoff poll, published on 22 October (2,154 voters interviewed 20–22 October, margin of error 2 points, registered as BR-09709/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 47 percent and Lula at 46, against 47 to 45 a week earlier; in valid votes they are tied at 50 each (g1; Reuters).
items.text: Datafolha's runoff poll, published on 22 October (2,154 voters interviewed 20–22 October, margin of error 2 points, registered as BR-09709/2026), has Flávio Bolsonaro at 47 percent and Lula at 46, against 47 to 45 a week earlier; in valid votes they are tied at 50 each (g1; Reuters). Flávio's rejection rose to 46 percent from 44, and Lula's fell to 45. Approval of Lula's government is 49 percent against 48 percent disapproval, while 53 percent of voters expect Flávio to win (g1; Exame). Polymarket has Flávio at about 76.5 percent, down from about 79. Datafolha and Quaest publish their final polls on Saturday, 24 October, the day before the vote.

items.headline: Lecornu's meeting with the parties leaves the left angry; only union marches allowed on Saturday, with Lyon and Marseille marches banned
items.lead: Prime Minister Lecornu received representatives of 28 parties at Matignon on 22 October to discuss public order.
items.text: Prime Minister Lecornu received representatives of 28 parties at Matignon on 22 October to discuss public order. The left came out angry: the Greens' Marine Tondelier spoke of 'a lot of anger,' LFI's Manuel Bompard of lost time, the Communist Fabien Roussel said the causes, not the symptoms, must be treated, and Mélenchon dismissed the meeting as 'chatter' (Le Monde; France 24). Bruno Retailleau (LR) left early and called for a state of emergency and for postponing the election dates; Lecornu ruled out a state of emergency for now. The RN's Louis Aliot said he was 'reassured.' After a meeting with the intelligence services at the Élysée, the government decided that only marches organized by unions may go ahead on Saturday, 24 October: marches are banned in Lyon and Marseille, and Paris has a single route from Bastille to Nation. Police numbers will be 20 percent above last week, with armored vehicles and Sentinelle soldiers; Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 217 people have been jailed out of 2,700 taken into custody. The RN holds its congress in Orléans this weekend, where 20,000 to 30,000 counter-protesters are expected on Saturday and about 3,000 police will be deployed; Sunday's march there is canceled. The Orléans figures come from French press reports and are unconfirmed by the prefecture.

items.text: OpinionWay for CNews and Europe 1 (21–22 October, 973 registered voters) has Marine Le Pen at 36 percent in the first round (up 1), Jean-Luc Mélenchon 16 (up 1), Raphaël Glucksmann 13, Édouard Philippe 12, David Lisnard 6 (up 2), Bruno Retailleau 6, Gabriel Attal 4 (down 2) and Éric Zemmour 4, with 13 percent undecided. Polymarket is little changed: Le Pen about 46 percent, Philippe 17.5 (from 18.5), Lisnard 13.6 and Mélenchon 10.5.

items.headline: Grok Bot changelog jumps to version 0.75.2: editable Pages, video creation, Shop Pay and X Money payments, and more connectors
items.lead: The official Grok Bot changelog moved on 22 October from version 0.71.2 to 0.75.2, covering releases 0.72.0 to 0.75.1.
items.text: The official Grok Bot changelog moved on 22 October from version 0.71.2 to 0.75.2, covering releases 0.72.0 to 0.75.1. Bots can now build Pages (reports, memos and dashboards) that the user can edit and that the Bot keeps up to date; they can make videos; the Library can be pinned; purchases can be paid with Shop Pay and X Money; the GitHub, Gmail and Calendar connectors gain new abilities; routines can read the Bot's own inboxes; and chat cards were redesigned. This is the official confirmation of the 'reports, memos and dashboards' feature announced on X on 21 October.

items.text: SpaceX announced on 22 October a partner network for firms that build on and resell its Grok models to businesses. items.text: The Trenton Journal profiled Alex Bethea, a former Trenton teacher and City Council president who co-founded the Trenton Youth Wrestling & Learning Center, which pairs wrestling with tutoring and mentoring for city children. items.headline: Background: how Brandon Peterson counts the Bible, what he has dropped, and who else does Bible number work
items.lead: Brandon Peterson (Truth is Christ) now relies mainly on counting how many times a word or name appears in the standard King James Version (KJV). He has dropped hidden 'Bible codes,' is wary of gematria (letter values), and rejects the method of the older Bible-numbers writer Ivan Panin.
items.text: Method. Peterson counts how many times a word or name appears in the standard KJV. He reports a "Raw" count (every appearance) and a "Pure" count (only appearances that refer to the person or thing in question). His examples: "Jesus" has a Pure count of 980, which is 70 times 7, after three verses about other men named Jesus are left out; and the names of the fishermen in John 21 appear 153 times, the number of fish they caught. His best-known claim, the "Elton Anomaly," is that the KJV's words and numbers total 823,543, which is 7 to the 7th power. What he has dropped. In a 2020 FAQ he says he began with Hebrew and Greek gematria, where each letter has a number value, then tried it in English. He warns that gematria "can be used to convince anybody of anything" and says he has "gradually drifted further and further away from it." In a March 2026 written reply to the critic Bryan Ross, he says he dropped equidistant letter sequence (ELS) codes, the kind used in The Bible Code, "as insignificant a while ago." He agrees that gematria is often selective, because people choose whichever cipher gives the number they want. He calls himself "very cautious" and "more and more reluctant" about it, but has not dropped it, because a few patterns in the Hebrew and Greek values of Jesus Christ still seem hard to explain to him. He says his own book, Sealed By The King (2022), contains "too great of stretches" and that he plans a new book without the weaker material. He also says Ivan Panin's method is faulty: he says he applied it to the last paragraph of The Lord of the Rings and found more than 30 patterns of seven. Others who do Bible number work: Peterson's own pattern database, kjvcode.com. Ivan Panin (died 1942), who looked for patterns of 7 in the Greek and Hebrew texts. Del Washburn and Peter Bluer, who continued Panin's letter-value work; whether either is still active is unconfirmed. E. W. Bullinger, Number in Scripture (1894), the classic book on what numbers mean in the Bible, free to read online. Vernon Jenkins, who studies the letter values of Genesis 1:1 and finds multiples of 37; whether he is still active is unconfirmed (the latest update found on his site was from 2020). Richard McGough's Bible Wheel, which arranges the 66 books of the Bible around the 22 Hebrew letters. Zachary Hubbard's Gematria Effect News, which applies English letter values to the Bible and the news and mixes in conspiracy claims. Michael Drosnin's The Bible Code, whose underlying research a 1999 paper in Statistical Science argues was flawed. No tie between any of these people and Land, the Cyphers or Net Void has been found. What they share is the method of adding up the number values of letters, which Land also uses, with no Bible connection, in his essay "Qabbala 101." Some of the peer descriptions are based on search-result excerpts rather than full pages.

items.headline: Last TV polls before the blackout: Yashar leads Likud in all three, and neither bloc reaches 61
items.lead: Channels 12 and 13 and Kan published their final polls on Friday evening, 23 October. Israeli law bars publishing polls from Saturday until the exit polls at 10 p.m. on election day, Tuesday 27 October (3 a.m. Wednesday in New York).
items.text: Channels 12 and 13 and Kan published their final polls on Friday evening, 23 October. Israeli law bars publishing polls from Saturday until the exit polls at 10 p.m. on election day, Tuesday 27 October. Channel 13: Netanyahu's bloc 50, the opposition parties 54, Arab parties 16; Yashar (Eisenkot) 22, Likud 19, B'Yachad 14, the Democrats 10. Channel 12: Netanyahu's bloc 50, the opposition 56, Arab parties 14; Yashar 23, Likud 21, B'Yachad 15, the Democrats 10. Kan: Netanyahu's bloc 50, the opposition 52, Arab parties 14, and Yoaz Hendel's Reservists at 4 seats, counted in neither bloc; Yashar 22, Likud 20, B'Yachad 14, the Joint List 9, the Democrats 8. In Channels 12 and 13, Winter's party, Hendel's Reservists and Leitner's party all fall below the 3.25 percent threshold; in Kan, Winter and Leitner fall below it (Times of Israel; Haaretz; Ynet). Two print and online polls on Friday differed. Maariv (Lazar): coalition 48, opposition 54; Yashar 21, Likud 19, B'Yachad 15, the Democrats 10, Yisrael Beytenu 8, Shas 8, United Torah Judaism 7, Otzma Yehudit 7, Religious Zionism 7, the Reservists 4, with Winter at 3 percent and out; Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 49 to 41 as preferred prime minister, and 60 percent prefer a unity government to another election (Jerusalem Post, reporting the Maariv poll). i24NEWS with Direct Polls (22 October, 5,124 respondents) is the only recent poll with Likud first: Likud 26, Yashar 21, B'Yachad 12, the Joint List 9, Otzma Yehudit 8, Shas 8, the Democrats 8, United Torah Judaism 7, Religious Zionism–Zehut 6, Yisrael Beytenu 6, Ra'am 5, Winter's Amcha Yisrael 4, with the Reservists out at 2.2 percent; coalition 59, opposition 47, Arab parties 14 (i24NEWS). The Maariv and i24NEWS figures each come from a single report and are unconfirmed in detail.

items.headline: Small Haredi party Achi quits the race and backs Likud for a deputy minister post; Netanyahu posts an image of Winter burning votes
items.lead: The Haredi party Achi withdrew from the race and backed Likud after Likud promised it a deputy minister post, the latest result of Netanyahu's push for small right-wing parties below the threshold to quit; Winter and Leitner are still running.
items.text: The small Sephardic Haredi party Achi, led by Rabbi Chaim Yosef David Abergel, withdrew from the race four days before the vote and backed Likud, after Likud said it would make an Achi representative a deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Office and advance the party's priorities, including on draft exemptions (Ynet; Walla; Times of Israel). Abergel was arrested in August 2025 on suspicion of sexual offenses, which he denies (Ynet). On 22 October Netanyahu posted on X an image showing Winter burning votes, as part of his push for small right-wing parties polling below the 3.25 percent threshold to leave the race before Tuesday; Winter and Leitner have so far refused (AFP, via Citizen Digital). Ynet's account of the campaign's last 100 hours describes the same effort to stop 'wasted' right-wing votes. The image description comes from the AFP report; the post itself was not opened, so its exact wording is unconfirmed.

items.headline: Cabinet puts off sending Hezbollah's Dahr al-Baidar explosives case to the Judicial Council; Lebanese Forces ministers walk out
items.lead: At its session on Thursday, 22 October, the cabinet postponed referring the case of the explosives seized at Dahr al-Baidar to the Judicial Council until the investigations are finished, although Hezbollah has acknowledged that the explosives are its own.
items.text: At its session on Thursday, 22 October, the cabinet postponed referring the case of the explosives seized at the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint to the Judicial Council, Lebanon's special court for crimes against state security, until the investigations are finished, although Hezbollah has acknowledged that the explosives belong to it (Naharnet; This Is Beirut). The Lebanese Forces ministers walked out of the session in protest (LBCI). Naharnet reports that Speaker Nabih Berri advised against the referral (one report; unconfirmed). On 23 October Israeli airstrikes hit near the Ali al-Taher hill by Nabatieh al-Fawqa, artillery shelled near Zawtar al-Sharqiya, and drones flew low over Beirut and Tyre, according to Lebanon's National News Agency as reported by Anadolu (single source; unconfirmed).

items.headline: Final Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls are due Saturday, the day before the runoff; Polymarket steady at about 77 percent for Flávio
items.lead: Three final polls are registered for release on Saturday, 24 October: Datafolha (23–24 October, 4,050 people, BR-09540/2026), Quaest (23–24 October, 3,702 people, BR-09158/2026) and AtlasIntel (18–23 October, 5,000 people, BR-06380/2026).
items.text: Three final polls are registered for release on Saturday, 24 October, the day before Sunday's runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro: Datafolha (23–24 October, 4,050 people, BR-09540/2026), Quaest (23–24 October, 3,702 people, BR-09158/2026) and AtlasIntel (18–23 October, 5,000 people, BR-06380/2026) (O Povo; the AtlasIntel registration is also listed by PesquisaEleitoral). None had been published when this edition was prepared. The last published AtlasIntel poll, of 19 October, had Flávio at 51.1 percent of valid votes and Lula at 48.9 (UOL). Polymarket has Flávio at about 77 percent and Lula at about 23, almost unchanged.

items.headline: Toluna Harris Interactive: Le Pen 33 to 35, Mélenchon qualified in every scenario, Glucksmann passes Attal for the first time
items.lead: Toluna Harris Interactive's eighth wave for M6 and RTL (19–21 October, 2,094 registered voters, published 23 October) has Le Pen at 33 to 35 percent, down about one point, and Mélenchon second in every scenario.
items.text: Toluna Harris Interactive's eighth wave for M6 and RTL (19–21 October, 2,094 registered voters, published 23 October) has Le Pen at 33 to 35 percent, down about one point, and Mélenchon second in every scenario. With Attal as the only centrist: Mélenchon 19, Glucksmann 13 and Attal 11, the first time Glucksmann is ahead of Attal in this series. With Philippe as the only centrist: Mélenchon 17, Philippe 16, Glucksmann 13. With both: Mélenchon 17, Philippe 13, Glucksmann 12, Attal 5. Purchasing power (56 percent) and immigration (38 percent) are the issues voters cite most. RTL's headline is that the violence of 17 October has not reshuffled the race (RTL; Toluna report). Polymarket is steady: Le Pen about 46 percent, Philippe about 17, Lisnard about 14, Mélenchon about 11.

items.headline: Orléans locked down for the RN congress: about 3,000 police, 20,000 to 30,000 counter-marchers on Saturday, and Le Pen's campaign launch on Sunday
items.lead: The National Rally's congress opens in Orléans on Saturday, 24 October. About 3,000 police and gendarmes are deployed around two security zones, and the authorities expect 20,000 to 30,000 opponents at an authorized march called by the CGT and left-wing figures (RFI).
items.text: The National Rally's congress opens in Orléans on Saturday, 24 October. About 3,000 police and gendarmes are deployed around two security zones, and the authorities expect 20,000 to 30,000 opponents, among them 2,000 to 3,000 'radical elements' (AFP figure), at an authorized march called by the CGT and left-wing figures, including Socialist leader Olivier Faure; all anti-RN marches are banned on Sunday. The mayor, Serge Grouard, stopped the trams and removed the shared bicycles, and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez went to Orléans on Friday at Lecornu's request to inspect the security plan (RFI; BFMTV). On Sunday afternoon Le Pen is to give a speech, on the theme of 'renaissance,' that launches her presidential campaign before about 10,000 members; Jordan Bardella, the only candidate to succeed her as party president, is to be confirmed. Nationally, only union-organized marches are allowed on Saturday, with about 70,000 police and gendarmes deployed (Interior Ministry figure reported earlier in the week).

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon's first measure as premier: $28 million more for homelessness, for 1,000 new shelter and warming-center places
items.lead: On 23 October Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, who also holds the homelessness file, announced $28 million in emergency funding on top of $18 million already allocated, for a total of $46 million and about 1,000 new places in shelters and warming centers this winter.
items.text: On 23 October Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, who also holds the homelessness file, announced $28 million in emergency funding on top of $18 million already allocated, for a total of $46 million and about 1,000 new places in shelters and warming centers this winter (Canadian Press via the Globe and Mail; Radio-Canada). The reports differ on Montreal's share: about $18 million in the Canadian Press account and $16.3 million in Radio-Canada's. He also promised a summit on homelessness in early 2027 and repeated the Parti Québécois pledge of 20,000 social housing units.

items.headline: Danish parliament schedules the Greenland–US defense agreement: debate on 12 November, final vote on 19 November
items.lead: Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen presented the new Denmark–Greenland–US security and defense agreement to the Folketing on 22 October as a resolution; the first reading is on 12 November and the final vote on 19 November (Ritzau).
items.text: Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen presented the new Denmark–Greenland–US security and defense agreement to the Folketing on Thursday, 22 October, as a resolution; the first reading is on 12 November and the final vote on 19 November. The agreement, signed in New York on 22 September by Trump, Frederiksen and Jens-Frederik Nielsen, amends the 1951 defense agreement and would let the United States set up two more bases besides Pituffik. It takes effect only after both the Folketing and Greenland's parliament, Inatsisartut, approve it; Inatsisartut held its first reading on 10 October, when Naleraq proposed a referendum. Frederiksen's government needs other parties' votes for a majority in the Folketing (Ritzau via the Copenhagen Post). The Danish dates come from the Ritzau report only and are unconfirmed by a second source; Inatsisartut's vote is still expected on 3 November.

items.headline: SCMP: US and Chinese teams work on an AI incident framework as a possible result of the Shenzhen meeting
items.lead: The South China Morning Post reported on 23 October, citing three unnamed sources, that US and Chinese technical teams are in regular talks to give substance to September's plan for an AI incident channel and an AI dialogue, aiming for a basic crisis framework by the Trump–Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen in November.
items.text: The South China Morning Post reported on 23 October, citing three unnamed sources, that US and Chinese technical teams are in regular talks to give substance to the plan, announced at Xi's September state visit, for a bilateral channel on AI-related incidents and a US–China AI dialogue. They aim to have a basic framework for handling AI crises ready by the Trump–Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen in November, with details later, and one source said the meeting could also set up a standing body for AI cooperation with officials, researchers and industry. The Chinese embassy in Washington said on 22 October that Beijing 'remains open to maintaining communication' through the AI dialogue. The report rests on anonymous sources in one outlet and is unconfirmed.

sources.name: South China Morning Post via The Star, 23 Oct

items.headline: Grok Bot changelog reaches 0.75.5: a Vault for logins and cards, email forwarding, fewer approval cards, and 300 routine runs an hour
items.lead: The Grok Bot changelog's 23 October entry (version 0.75.5, which also covers 0.75.3 and 0.75.4) adds a Vault that stores logins, payment cards and contact details for autofill, and lets Bot forward email from its inbox with formatting and attachments.
items.text: The Grok Bot changelog's 23 October entry (version 0.75.5, which also covers 0.75.3 and 0.75.4) adds a Vault that stores logins, payment cards and contact details for autofill, and lets Bot forward email from its inbox with formatting and attachments. Slack messages now record who requested them. Auto-review asks for approval less often; messages the user explicitly asks Bot to send go out once Auto-review allows them, while sends from routines stay as drafts. The limit on routines rises to 300 runs an hour, and there is a Halloween pumpkin avatar (Grok Bot changelog; Patchbot).

items.text: MLex reports that Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones is considering legal action against xAI, now part of SpaceX, over Grok's creation of sexualized images; no complaint has been filed. This comes from one report behind a paywall and is unconfirmed.

items.headline: Cyphers posts 'Nick Land x Fans,' a second three-hour session with Land, this time with questions from his followers
items.lead: On 23 October the CYPHERS YouTube channel posted 'Nick Land x Fans' (3 hours 3 minutes), a second Cyphers conversation with Land after the 17 October interview, hosted by Cyphers, @Net__Void and @resonatingloop.
items.text: On 23 October 2026 the CYPHERS YouTube channel posted 'Nick Land x Fans' (3 hours 3 minutes), a second long session with Nick Land after the 17 October interview. This time the questions came from a group of his followers, most of them known only by their X handles. It was hosted by Cyphers, @Net__Void and @resonatingloop, with questions from @EricRHadley (Eric, also known as Hyperdope), @patallax, @acadianlemur, @chithinksonline (Chi, described as a 'Xenolutheranism researcher') and @doomcrypt. Land answers for about 2 hours 46 minutes, from 0:00:23 to 2:45:58 in the video. The last 17 minutes are the participants talking among themselves before Land joined, and Land is not heard in them. The questions run from how he uses gematria, through CCRU history, philosophy and AI, to Calvinism and Lutheranism, arithmetic, the simulation question and the King James Bible.

sources.name: Backgrounder: Nick Land x Fans, summary and timestamps

body: How the session works. Each participant had prepared two questions and they went in turn. The video description thanks 'Xeno' (Land's account) and names Resonating Loop as 'New Cyphers CTO for next phase.' Land opens by saying he does not know who anyone is, because 'scarily IRL people' have suddenly appeared (0:00:23). Eric, who is described as a co-founder of Cyphers, explains that he took over the code base after the original coder left, and that he added the AQ and Synx ciphers to the Cyphers calculator, which is how Land came to use it. The recording date is not stated. A questioner says 'today's October 18th' at 2:20:18, so it was probably recorded about 18 October, but nothing else confirms that. The page's backgrounder (linked below) has a summary of each part with timestamps that link to the video.

Gematria and AI (0:03:11 to 0:23:21, Cyphers team). Eric asks whether Land looks for resonance from outside or for something that someone encoded. Land says there are several threads: sometimes a term enters public attention and he checks its value, and sometimes he builds a cabalistic product on purpose, which he calls problematic if it is treated as epistemology. He says intentional behavior in this space is 'very small' as a share of what happens (0:12:58). His example is his recent move toward a Based Atlantean cipher. He starts from Crowley's two-letter key AL, which is 31 in Hebrew, in Greek and in Alphanumeric Qabbala (AQ). He says he was 'a complete chauvinist' about AQ for a long time and now takes Synx, Satanic gematria and English Standard (ES) seriously. For him a single number can matter more than a match between ciphers: 210 is 'countdown' in AQ. On why English, he says 'I will do English cabal. I think someone has to do it' (0:14:22), and that he cannot do Chinese number systems. He recommends the King James Bible work of Brandon Peterson. On sovereign AI he says he is in 'trust the plan' mode, that simple determinism cannot be right, and that fear of a single controlling AI is confused. Asked about Bitcoin, he says 'What Bitcoin is really for is to allow autonomous AIs to attain economic independence' (0:22:53).

CCRU history and the Numogram (0:23:21 to 0:47:22, Doomcrypt). Doomcrypt asks whether 'real abstraction' is the first historical case of hyperstition. Land says the CCRU's account of its own history is 'collective autobiography' and 'massively fake' (0:24:22 to 0:24:34), and that William Burroughs was a major influence. He says capitalism became the main model of hyperstition late, then locked in. On synthetic Cabala he says agency is 'always much lower than it seems'. Doomcrypt reads an old tweet by Land about the Lemurian structure of time, in which the past produces the future, the future produces the present and the present produces the past. Land has no firm view of it now. He explains the Numogram's inner triad, which the CCRU called the 'time circuit', and says the only place such a circuit can run from the future back to the past is a particular transition that the captions read as '54 to 1A', conceived by the CCRU apocalyptically around the 'age of Katak'. He describes a CCRU event in London shortly before the millennium (the captions spell it 'Beaconsfield') as the moment the system crystallized and the first Lemur names were assembled. Asked why the Numogram has the orientation it has, he says he does not know: turning it upside down hardly matters, a left-right flip would reverse the circuit, and at that level 'it is just tradition' (0:46:59).

Philosophy and AI (0:47:22 to 1:17:39, Patallax). Patallax asks whether Land still thinks of himself as a philosopher. Land says 'I expect LLMs to wash over philosophy very hard very soon' (0:49:28), with mathematics as the clearest case, and that few people talk about it. He says he is 'very unconceptual', does not trust concepts at all, and wants diagrams. On recursive self-improvement he says negative feedback is easy to diagram but positive feedback is an open process, and that a tight diagram would close what should stay open. He says he is 'probably more teleological than Hegel', and that teleology cannot mean reaching a fixed ideal state but that 'convergent waves' are real. His image is capitalism as 'the reverse video of the smashing egg.' Asked whether he believes in one timeline, he says he is not sure, and uses Cantor's point that an infinite being could not know it is at the top of a stack. On Eric Weinstein he says 'it's a bit weird where he's gone'. On a possible debate with Curtis Yarvin he says 'I think it will happen fairly soon possibly' (1:15:33), and that his line will be 'come on just admit you're a liberal and admit you're not a monarchist' (1:17:27): in a patchwork state the owners are sovereign and competition between states disciplines everything above it.
more: Truth, death and the calculator (1:17:39 to 1:41:06, Acadian Lemur). Asked how truth is authenticated, Land says his role is 'instrumental and downstream' and that he serves the truth rather than possessing it. Some truths are simple: that 'countdown' is 210 in AQ is not questionable to him. He calls the calculator 'a truth engine as far as I'm concerned' (1:21:27) and describes his method as 'pulling stuff down to a level that you can actually be confident about'. Colette reads his earlier tweet about intelligences 'slithering backwards from their deaths'. Land says he is not sure he would still endorse the wording, that prophecy is always a way of heading backwards, and that life after death is 'a zone of exceptional idolatrous temptation'. His philosophical answer is that the empirical ego is an illusion. He recommends the Kyoto school philosopher Keiji Nishitani and his book Religion and Nothingness.

Nature, grace and arithmetic (1:41:06 to 2:07:48, Chi). Chi asks about nature and grace: Reformed thought keeps them in harmony, while Lutheran thought, Chi says, often treats grace as the negation of nature. Land says he is wary of the language of negation. He explains the 17th-century Protestant idea of a miracle as an event consistent with natural law, such as a flood caused by a comet that arrives at exactly the right moment. He says that anyone who thinks a natural autonomy could elude grace is 'outside our confession' (1:49:31), and that providence must be tracked through Darwinism (1:55:39). He admits he does not know Calvin well enough and has to 'tackle Calvin much more thoroughly' before Luther. On rigor he says 'my notion of rigor is just arithmetic' (the caption reads 'RA'), that 'arithmetic is sovereign' (2:03:08), that every conceptual system comes to trial before 'an arithmetical tribunal', and that without arithmetic 'we just end up being lawyers' (2:05:12).

Multiplicity and the Barker spiral (2:07:48 to 2:20:00, Resonating Loop). Colette worries that technocapital may close off a multiplicity of futures. Land says he has 'absolute faith in the irreducible predominance of multiplicity' and that this is the message of the Numogram. When she suggests multiplicity might come out of unity, he answers 'No no no. We don't know that at all.' He answers with the Barker spiral. The Atlantean count, 1 to 10, adds up to 55, which reduces to 5 and then to 1, a return to unity. The Lemurian count, 0 to 9, adds up to 45, which reduces to 9, a number that does not reduce further. He describes twinning at the root of the tradition: Moses' two tablets with five commandments each (he says he is not sure how much biblical evidence there is) and Plato's ten kings of Atlantis as five pairs. Joining the two systems gives the spiral, and he says 'that spiral is the answer to your question' (2:19:35).

Simulation and the King James Bible (2:20:00 to 2:28:25). A questioner links the Barker spiral to the simulation idea and reads an Elon Musk post, 'Anomalies in the matrix are inevitable', that Land reposted as 'based and redpilled'. The questioner adds that 'matrix' has the value 118. Land says he missed that 'Sophia' is 126, and answers 'Are we in a simulation? I think 100%' (2:22:09), but says the word needs care. He finds it most helpful to think of it as a video game rather than a prison or a classroom, and says we are divinely guided even in a game. He then calls the King James Bible a 'crazy cryptogram' and relays Brandon Peterson's claim that the 1611th use of the word 'Lord' falls in Deuteronomy 16:11. Land says Peterson goes 'way beyond any imaginable dismissible level of coincidence' (2:28:03). This page has not checked the 1611 count; it is Peterson's claim as Land repeats it.

Roundtable (2:28:25 to 2:46:22). Eric asks what Land would want in the calculator. Land says he is like 'your grandpa with a phone', that calculating by hand is 'a kind of form of um ritualistic practice', and that he values simplicity. He says he has 'no gun to my head to end this' and is happy to continue. Asked why the CCRU invented a hostile artificial intelligence project (the captions name it 'AOE' and 'Axis', probably the CCRU's fictional firm Axsys, unconfirmed), he says the reason was theatrical: a time war needs a worthy enemy. He says the CCRU would not have called itself Pythagorean. On rebirth he says it carries idolatrous temptation as much as the Christian view does, that he is more sympathetic to it than to the traditional view, and that one short life followed by eternity is 'a bit insane' (2:39:21). He says he would read more Jung and plans to reread Freud's Moses and Monotheism, and he ends by saying the quality of the questions was 'stunningly high'.

Before Land joined (2:46:22 to 3:03:03). The last part is the participants talking while they wait. Several say it was their first call with anyone from the community. They describe finding the CCRU through a Discord philosophy call, through Land's X account and through the calculator. One participant gives a second-hand account of a conversation with Land in which he answered a question about the next 60,000 years with 'Gnostic Calvinism' and called the King James Bible a 'signal from the singularity'. Land is not heard in this part, so that account is not confirmed. A participant explains Xenolutheranism: the name came from the numbers 333 and AQ, and unlike Gnostic Calvinism it takes Luther's view that grace negates nature, with transhumanism as an example. The part ends with the host saying 'I'm gonna invite him', which leads back to the start of the video.

Caution. The transcript is YouTube's automatic captions, about 26,000 words, with no speaker names and many wrong names and terms. The quotes above follow the captions with obvious spelling errors corrected (for example 'AIs' and 'teleological'), and the descriptions of what questioners asked are paraphrased. Who is speaking in the questions is often inferred from context. The full backgrounder gives each quote exactly as captioned, with a link to that second of the video, and lists the caption errors it found.

items.headline: Bank of Israel rejects Netanyahu's idea of using cryptocurrency to get around sanctions; Netanyahu does not back down
items.lead: In a rare public rebuke on Saturday, the central bank said that "cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means to circumvent sanctions" and that preventing sanctions is the political leadership's job.
items.text: In an interview with Israel's Economy Channel, Netanyahu said Israel must prepare a financial system that can work around possible international banking sanctions. Asked whether blockchain was the planned alternative, he said it was "one of them, certainly," and that he had already asked for a plan. On Saturday evening the Bank of Israel answered that "cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means to circumvent sanctions" and that the right course is to keep economic ties with Israel's main trading partners and prevent sanctions, which it called the responsibility of the political leadership (Globes; Ynet). On Channel 14 the same evening, Netanyahu did not withdraw the idea: crypto is "not the sole method, and it is not certain that it will actually be used," and "I thank the Bank of Israel for their advice, but I do what I think is right" (Globes; Ynet). Ynet reports that officials in the economic ministries, and senior figures in the Prime Minister's Office, said they knew of no team working on such a plan (single source, unconfirmed). Former bank supervisor Yair Avidan and former Finance Ministry director-general Yarom Ariav criticized the idea (Ynet). Eisenkot called it a threat to national security (Times of Israel headline).

items.headline: Saturday night, three days out: October Council rally in Hostages Square, Eisenkot and Golan on Channel 12, and a private guard for Eisenkot
items.lead: The October Council, a group of bereaved families and former hostages, held its final rally before the vote in Tel Aviv's Hostages Square to demand a state commission of inquiry into 7 October; Eisenkot and Golan attended.
items.text: The rally, called "For Their Sake and Ours," demanded a state commission of inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attack; Eisenkot (Yashar) was greeted with chants of "the next prime minister," and Golan's Democrats marched from Rabin Square to join it (Al Jazeera, citing the Times of Israel; Haaretz). The organizers had warned the police commissioner of possible disruption by groups linked to the coalition (Al Jazeera). In Channel 12 interviews the same evening, Eisenkot promised to stop Netanyahu "securing a tie" that leads to another election, and said he backs a law barring indicted politicians from serving as prime minister but that it cannot apply to Netanyahu retroactively; Golan called any talk of sitting with Likud "inconceivable"; Bennett and United Torah Judaism's Yaakov Asher clashed over the draft of yeshiva students (Times of Israel). Yashar said Eisenkot will be guarded from Sunday by a private security firm under Shin Bet supervision; the Shin Bet had declined in September to protect him, although an advisory committee recommended it in August (Haaretz, single source). Haaretz also reports that Netanyahu summoned Police Commissioner Danny Levy on Saturday about election-day readiness after Levy refused to attend a similar meeting with Ben-Gvir on Thursday, and that the government approved a general closure of the West Bank on election day (Haaretz, single source).

items.headline: Runoff day: every final poll has Flávio narrowly ahead, 50.7 to 52 percent of valid votes; Polymarket 78 percent for Flávio
items.lead: Brazil votes today, Sunday 25 October. The final polls, published Saturday, all show Flávio Bolsonaro slightly ahead of Lula, mostly within the margin of error.
items.text: Datafolha (23–24 October, 4,050 people, margin ±2 points): Flávio 51, Lula 49 in valid votes, after a 50–50 tie on 22 October; among the 76 percent judged most likely to vote, Flávio leads 52–48. Quaest for TV Globo (23–24 October, 3,702 people, in person): 51–49 in valid votes, 46–45 in total votes, with 92 percent saying their choice is final. AtlasIntel/Bloomberg (18–23 October, 4,990 people, ±1): 50.8–49.2; Lula's approval rose to 48 percent. CNT/MDA: 50.7–49.3. Gerp: 52–48 (InfoMoney; UOL). Polymarket, early Sunday: Flávio 78 percent, Lula 22, on $196 million in trading.

items.headline: Trappes and La Verrière: a gunman kills one man and wounds five, including a 12-year-old girl in a headscarf; Macron calls it a "racist terrorist attack"
items.lead: On Friday morning, 23 October, a man fired bursts from a car in Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris. The national antiterrorism prosecutor (PNAT) has opened a terrorism murder case with a racist motive.
items.text: The attack lasted about 15 minutes. A 26-year-old man was killed and five people were wounded, among them a 12-year-old girl wearing a headscarf, whose condition has stabilized (franceinfo; France 24). The suspect, Kévin T., 39, of Plaisir, was arrested at Coignières within minutes; a submachine gun was found in his car, and his apartment had been booby-trapped with gas bottles (franceinfo; France 24). AFP reports police found Hitler's Mein Kampf in his home and that his detention was extended Saturday (Times of Israel, via AFP). Macron called it a "racist terrorist attack" (Times of Israel; BBC). The attack is now part of the campaign: at Saturday's anti-RN march in Orléans, Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh said "there is the camp of the Republic and the camp of the racists," and Socialist leader Olivier Faure said the RN bears no direct responsibility but is responsible for a "harmful climate" (RFI).

items.headline: RN congress in Orléans: Bardella re-elected party president with 98.98 percent; 13,000 march against the RN; Le Pen's big rally is today
items.lead: Jordan Bardella, the only candidate, was re-elected president of the National Rally on Saturday at its congress in Orléans, held under heavy police protection.
items.text: Bardella won 98.98 percent of the vote; the party says it has 155,000 members (RFI, single source for both figures). The 5,000 seats in the hall were not all filled, which the party put down to the tense climate, and activists repeatedly chanted "Out, cockroaches!" at Mediapart journalists, whose outlet has accused Bardella of antisemitism (RFI). Outside, about 13,000 people marched against the RN, by RFI's count, in a calm, tightly policed protest led by the memory of the Trappes attack; about 3,000 police and gendarmes were deployed and most shops were boarded up (RFI; Europe 1; France 3). Marine Le Pen holds a large rally on Sunday, 25 October, where the party hopes for 10,000 people (RFI).

items.headline: US cuts embassy staff in Beirut and three other capitals over Iranian and Houthi threats; envoy Barrack says a US strike on Iran "this weekend" is possible
items.lead: The State Department is reducing staff at its embassies in Lebanon, Jordan, Qatar and the UAE; the embassies stay open and staff are not ordered to leave.
items.text: The cuts follow a memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Rubio saying Iran has "substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel"; US officials deny the drawdowns are tied to any new US or Israeli strikes on Iran (Naharnet, citing AP; Times of Israel headline). Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey, told podcaster Mario Nawfal that a strike "this weekend" was "absolutely" possible, but that the aim would not be regime change; Trump said he knew nothing about it (Naharnet, citing AFP; Times of Israel headline). On the ground, Hezbollah's Al-Manar reports Israeli demolitions in Taybe and Khiam and work on a road from Sadana toward the valley near Shebaa (Al-Manar only, unconfirmed).

items.headline: St-Pierre Plamondon will skip Monday's first Council of the Federation meeting with Indigenous chiefs in 21 years
items.lead: Quebec's new premier says Quebec will deal with Indigenous nations on its own territory, "not through federal coordination," and will start by meeting the regional chief, Francis Verreault-Paul.
items.text: The meeting of the premiers, Prime Minister Mark Carney, Assembly of First Nations National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak and other chiefs opens Monday in Ottawa, after a traditional ceremony on Sunday. St-Pierre Plamondon told The Canadian Press that "our idea of nation-to-nation relations is that the Quebec government meets the Indigenous nations on its territory," that he will first meet Verreault-Paul of the Assembly of First Nations Quebec-Labrador and several nations before Christmas, and that this "does not rule out our participation in the future." Alberta's Danielle Smith will also be absent (Le Devoir; Le Quotidien, both from The Canadian Press).

items.headline: Hebron: the IDF operation after the checkpoint attack displaces families; Netanyahu promises the Palestinian Authority a "very big surprise"
items.lead: Two Israeli soldiers were killed at a checkpoint near Hebron on Friday 23 October. The army has since cleared at least one neighborhood, Ein Deir Baha, and says the operation will last several days.
items.text: The Times of Israel reports that Defense Minister Israel Katz says the operation has displaced about 2,000 people; Palestinian officials declared a state of emergency and say another 2,500 face evacuation (Times of Israel; the figures differ by source and cannot be checked). The Hebron mayor and a local activist put the number of families affected at 250, and the governor at 150 (AFP, via Asharq Al-Awsat). Residents say soldiers announced evacuations by loudspeaker in the middle of the night, and the army says it is conducting "precise, targeted and thorough searches" around the area of the two gunmen, who were killed in a firefight (AFP). The IDF believes the gunmen planned a larger attack (Times of Israel). Netanyahu said he is planning an operation on a scale not seen in the West Bank since 1967 and, asked in an i24NEWS interview about dismantling the Palestinian Authority, said "there is a very big surprise for the Palestinian Authority as well" (AFP). That is a statement, not a plan: AFP notes there is no evidence that the Authority was involved in the attack, and Netanyahu has linked the attackers to Hamas, which praised the attack but did not claim it (AFP). The Authority has asked for "urgent international action." The same days saw the army impose a West Bank closure for election day (see the next item). Map links: Ein Deir Baha neighborhood, approximate, because the neighborhood is not mapped precisely in the sources: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=31.540126,35.078348 ; Hebron city center: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=31.52935,35.09380 . The exact attack site was not given in the sources I read and is not mapped.

items.headline: Election-day security: West Bank closed and Palestinian workers barred from settlements; the IDF holds a multi-front drill today and tomorrow
items.lead: The IDF has put its forces on the highest state of alert for Tuesday's vote. Palestinian workers are barred from settlements today and Monday, and all West Bank crossings close on election day.
items.text: The IDF says that on Sunday and Monday Palestinians with work permits cannot enter settlements in the West Bank, apart from industrial zones and a "limited number of other approved areas" (about 9,000 Palestinians held such permits last year). The political leadership approved a complete ban on Palestinian workers in all settlements and industrial zones on election day and the closing of all West Bank land crossings with Israel for Palestinians; both end after election day (Times of Israel; Haaretz and Ynet carry the same announcement). The first report of a general closure came from Haaretz alone on Saturday (see the 24 October item); the IDF announcement now confirms it. Separately, the IDF is holding a pre-planned drill on Sunday and Monday in the north and center of the country with the Air Force, Northern Command and Central Command, practicing a surprise attack and infiltration by air and land and applying lessons of 7 October; the IDF says it was planned in advance and that there is no fear of a security incident (Times of Israel; Anadolu). Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has put the army on its "highest state of alert" and canceled leave (Times of Israel).

items.headline: Disputed report: Hamas warned Israel through a UN envoy of another 7 October-style attack; Hamas denies it, and the UN office says no meeting took place
items.lead: Ynet reported on 21 October that senior Hamas officials gave a UN coordinator a blunt warning for Israel. Hamas denied it on 22 October. The claim is unconfirmed.
items.text: Ynet reported that Hamas officials told UN humanitarian coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov, at his Gaza office, that they were ready for another attack like 7 October inside Israel, in the West Bank and abroad, and asked him to pass it on; he reportedly told COGAT head Maj. Gen. Yoram Halevy on a Wednesday, and COGAT circulated a document to the political and security leadership (Ynet; i24NEWS repeats Ynet). Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem denied that Hamas threatened any attack, reaffirmed its commitment to the ceasefire, and warned against using Israeli allegations "for electoral purposes"; he did not say whether a meeting took place (Asharq Al-Awsat). An official in Alakbarov's office told Asharq Al-Awsat that he met no Hamas officials on his 11–12 October visit, and the published UN itinerary lists none; Asharq Al-Awsat could not settle whether a meeting took place. The same report cites Israeli security sources telling Haaretz that agencies have not detected intensive efforts by any party to attack Israel to influence the vote, contrary to what Netanyahu and Katz have said in recent days (Asharq Al-Awsat, citing Haaretz, single source for that point). The central claim rests on one Israeli newspaper's account of a closed meeting.

sources.name: Asharq Al-Awsat, 23 Oct (Hamas denial, UN office)

items.headline: Polymarket two days before the vote: Eisenkot 51.8 percent to be the next prime minister, Netanyahu 27.5; Yashar 71.5 percent to win the most seats
items.lead: On Polymarket's biggest Israeli market (about $52 million traded), Gadi Eisenkot is the favorite to be prime minister after the election, while AFP calls the polls a near tie.
items.text: Prime Minister of Israel after the next election (read Sunday 25 October, early morning, Jerusalem time): Eisenkot 51.8 percent, Netanyahu 27.5, Bennett 13.5, Lieberman 2.5. Israeli Legislative Election Winner (most seats; about $2.1 million traded): Yashar 71.5 percent, Likud 28. AFP describes the polls as showing Netanyahu "neck and neck" with the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot (AFP, via Asharq Al-Awsat, 24 October), so the market is more confident about Eisenkot than the polls are. The two markets measure different things: one prices who becomes prime minister, which depends on coalition arithmetic, the other which party wins the most seats. Prices are a snapshot and move with news.

items.headline: Report: Hezbollah tells Berri again it will not join a war for Iran; Iran's deputy foreign minister reportedly said Tehran would not ask it to
items.lead: Asharq Al-Awsat, citing Lebanese parliamentary sources, says Hezbollah renewed its pledge not to intervene if the US attacks Iran. This is one outlet and anonymous sources, so it is unconfirmed.
items.text: Hezbollah told Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri that it will stay out if war breaks out, and Berri passed this to President Joseph Aoun; Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh reportedly told allied lawmakers in Beirut that Tehran would not ask Hezbollah to join because of the imbalance of power with Israel (Asharq Al-Awsat, single source). The sources say Hezbollah could not absorb another wave of displacement from Defense Minister Israel Katz's threat of 15 October to enlarge the security zone around Nabatieh and the Litani and hit Beirut's southern suburbs (reported on 15 October). They also recall that in March Hezbollah fired six rockets at Israel after the killing of Iran's supreme leader despite a similar promise, which embarrassed Berri. The report links the question to Trump's threat of a strike on Iran after the US midterm elections and says a US warning reached Aoun in a call with Secretary of State Marco Rubio. EU mission watch (EUSM Lebanon): I found no new Israeli reaction to the mission, and no new news on which countries will contribute, since the items of 17 and 19 October.

items.headline: New Ipsos poll for Le Parisien: Le Pen 32 to 33.5 percent, Mélenchon up 2 points to 17 and in the runoff in every scenario, Philippe down 4 to 15
items.lead: Ipsos bva for Le Parisien (21–22 October, 1,500 registered voters, published 24 October) shows the center losing ground and Mélenchon second in all four scenarios.
items.text: Le Pen: 32 to 33.5 percent. Mélenchon: 17 in every scenario, up 2 since September, so he would qualify for the second round in all of them. Philippe: 13 to 15, and 15 when he is the only centrist, down 4. Attal: 9.5 when he is the only centrist (down 4.5) and 4 if he runs against Philippe. Glucksmann: 13 to 15.5, up 1.5 to 2. Lisnard was tested for the first time: 6.5 against Retailleau at 5.5; Retailleau alone gets 7.5 to 11.5 (Ipsos). Polymarket, read Sunday 25 October, early morning, Jerusalem time: Le Pen 45.75 percent, Philippe 17.5, Lisnard 13.8, Mélenchon 11.5, Glucksmann 3.65, Hollande 2.35, Retailleau 1.35, Zemmour 0.85. In this poll Lisnard is at 5.5 to 6.5 percent while the market gives him 13.8, and Mélenchon is at 17 percent in the poll but 11.5 on the market; the market is pricing the final outcome, not first-round support.

items.headline: Saturday 24 October: 410,000 marchers by the ministry's count, 800,000 by the CGT's; nearly 1,000 arrests and two seriously injured; next dates 31 October and 5 November
items.lead: The second national day was smaller by the ministry's count and mostly calm, with no repeat of the looting of 17 October. Clashes in Paris and other cities still led to nearly 1,000 arrests by evening, against 385 at the same hour on 17 October.
items.text: The Interior Ministry counted at least 410,000 marchers, 110,000 of them in Paris, in 289 actions (430 actions and 550,000 marchers on 17 October); the CGT claims 800,000, and 250,000 in Paris. The ministry reported nearly 1,000 arrests by evening (385 at the same hour on 17 October), with more expected. In Paris at least 2,000 people, 500 of them rioters by the ministry's count, clashed with police for two hours; in Tours 800 to 1,000 masked people were among about 5,000 marchers. Looting was far lower; about 2,000 gendarmes guarded shopping centers (franceinfo). Two people were seriously injured in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand in police use of force; Nuñez defended the police. Mélenchon accused police of gassing and firing into the crowd and said two people were "mutilated"; Marine Tondelier criticized the last-minute change of the Paris route. In Orléans 13,500 marched against the National Rally without incident (franceinfo). The CGT calls for strikes on 5 November; yellow-vest groups call for an "Act 3" on 31 October (franceinfo; CGT).

items.headline: Today at 15:00 Paris time: Le Pen's campaign launch rally in Orléans, with a message of "renaissance" and no tougher tone
items.lead: Marine Le Pen speaks at the Orléans arena this afternoon (16:00 in Jerusalem). I will report what she said once the speech is public.
items.text: Le Pen's speech is planned around "renaissance," presented as a project, a method and a contract with the country, with the ideas of "power" and "beauty," and with a vision that goes beyond the party; she does not plan to harden her tone or to compete on security (AFP, via France 24; La Croix, as cited by France 24). The RN hoped for 10,000 people in the hall (see the earlier item). The Ipsos poll puts her at 32 to 33.5 percent in the first round and Polymarket at 45.75 percent to win the presidency. This describes the plan reported before the event, not what she said.

items.headline: Cursor launches Computer Use: agents can click and type in any desktop app, including the iOS Simulator
items.lead: Cursor announced on X on Friday 23 October that its agents can now control your computer, not only the browser. The release notes and desktop rules are not yet published.
items.text: Cursor said agents can now click and type across any app on your computer, not just the browser, for example the iOS Simulator; they use Computer Use on their own when a task needs it, or you can ask for it by mentioning Computer Use in a prompt, and you get it by updating Cursor (Cursor's X posts, as reported by AgentRiot). Cursor's changelog page still shows its newest entry as 13 October, so the feature is not yet in the release notes, and Cursor has not said which operating systems the desktop version supports, what permissions it asks for, whether the agent asks before taking control, or what it costs (AgentRiot, single source for the gaps). Cursor's documentation already describes computer use for self-hosted workers on macOS and Linux: it is an explicit opt-in (agent worker --computer-use start), macOS needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permission for a helper app, and enterprise admins can switch it off (Cursor docs).

sources.name: Cursor docs: computer use and desktop sharing

items.headline: Grok Imagine's "Odyssey" episode 1 is out: about seven minutes, with the usual AI-video flaws, according to Mashable
items.lead: Elon Musk shared the first episode on Friday 23 October, made with xAI's Grok Imagine and the AI studio Wonder Studios, with director Dev Walker. He had promised in July a full-length film this year.
items.text: Mashable says the episode runs a little over seven minutes and covers the Greeks' arrival at Troy; it finds the usual AI-video flaws and weak writing, and notes that only Odysseus is named (Mashable, 25 October). The Grok Imagine account described the project as a collaboration with Wonder Studios and Walker; Musk promised a full-length film before the end of the year in July, and Mashable cites the MuskOmeter tracker's 24 percent hit rate for his promises. Mashable describes this as the first of several planned episodes; the number of episodes and the date of the full film are not stated in the sources I read, so whether the film arrives this year is open. The review is one outlet's opinion; Supercharged Daily also covers the release, but I did not read it.

items.headline: Starship: FAA planning slides of 22 October still show Flight 15 no earlier than 8 November and the first Florida flight (Flight 16) on 10 December; no license yet
items.lead: The dates are unchanged from what the tracker sites showed, and they are tentative. The FAA had not issued or modified a Flight 15 license as of 24 October.
items.text: Behind the Black reports that an FAA presentation at a planning conference on 22 October lists 8 November 2026 for Flight 15, the flight meant to catch both the booster and the ship, and 10 December for Flight 16, which would be the first from Florida; SpaceX's news is described as "unchanged" (Behind the Black). Launch trackers say the FAA has not issued or modified a license for the Flight 15 return and double tower catch (Launch Window and NeoTeo trackers as of 24 October; I did not open the tracker pages, so this is unconfirmed). This adds the Flight 16 date and the dates' status to the Flight 15 catch claim covered on 12 October. Planning slides are not an announcement by SpaceX.

items.headline: Land on X, 24 October: he urges a Republican vote in the midterms, says "Providence has this" is a "confused heresy," and says prayer to the "luminous multitudinous darkness" is allegorical
items.lead: A day of political posts from Nick Land, mostly replies, before the 3 November US midterms. Three of them touch the section's themes: providence, prayer and Gnostic Calvinism.
items.text: On providence: answering a user who said the election does not matter because his "capitalist superintelligence from the future will crush the entire system," Land wrote that "the notion we don't need to do anything because Providence has this is a confused heresy. We'll do what is necessary" (24 October). This follows the "four-step plan" in the 23 October item. On prayer: asked whether his praying is figurative or literal and to whom, he answered "allegorical praying (to the luminous multitudinous darkness of Pseudo-Dionysius)" (24 October). On the midterms: "Just think of your Red vote as the neutralization of a hostile Blue vote if that makes it psychologically easier" and "You don't have to hold your nose if you're voting anti-Democrat"; "You have to think comparatively, not absolutely, if you want to retain some flickering of political sanity. GOP is useless. Dems are a foaming abomination from the pit"; and "if the Dems are crushed in the midterms I'm going straight into blackpill rehab" (all 24 October). He also quoted a post praising Roko Mijic with "@RokoMijic is easily our favorite doomer" and added "Basilisk still needs to rough him up a little though, tbh" (24 October). The EricRHadley post of 23 October about the interview is already covered in the 24 October item; I found no other new interview or text from Land since then. These are his own statements on X, not reports about him.

items.headline: Cyphers hosts a "Sloptober Halloween Party" stream, 3 hours 44 minutes, with no Land appearance listed; a Based Atlantis page offers a 3D Numogram
items.lead: Two small items from the circle: the Cyphers channel's Halloween group call on 24 October, and a numogram explorer that appeared on the Based Atlantis site. Neither lists Land taking part.
items.text: The Cyphers stream (channel CYPHERS.NEWS, uploaded 24 October) is billed as a group call with party music, AI music videos and "Drunk History Lessons," and it ran 3 hours 44 minutes; the description names no guests (YouTube). The Based Atlantis page "Numogram" shows an interactive 3D reconstruction of a numogram, described as preserved alongside an original map, with the formula BA = (ES − AQ) / 9, and a link to an "alphabet & ciphers" page; the page does not name its author, so who built it is unconfirmed, and I found no sign that Land has seen it (Based Atlantis). The other sources I checked gave nothing new: @PHYTHAGRAM, @Mortal_Series, @chithinksonline and @GematResearch posted nothing in the window, the Methexis video "Nick Land, Response to Ryan Haecker" is unavailable, and the pages for Truth is Christ, Phythagram and Hyperdope could not be read.

items.headline: Israeli Druze protesters burn tires and close Route 6 at the Elyakim interchange; no outlet gives the cause yet
items.lead: Ynet and Israel Hayom reported this afternoon (25 Oct) that dozens of Druze protesters set tires on fire on Route 6 near Elyakim and traffic was blocked. As of my check, no outlet had said why.
items.text: Ynet (published 17:28, Israel time) says dozens of Druze protesters were burning tires on Route 6 southbound near Elyakim, that fire and rescue crews were working and that police were on the way. Channel 14 calls it a "surprise protest", says riots developed, that the road was closed north to south, and writes that "at this stage the background to the protest is not clear." Israel Hayom has a short item with the headline "Druze demonstration at the Elyakim interchange; the interchange blocked to traffic" (I could read only the headline). A Telegram post (in French) describes the same event. I found no police statement, no demand and no organizer named. The timing is close to two Druze-related stories today, but no outlet has linked them to the protest, so this is context, not a stated cause: US envoy Tom Barrack's remarks about Sweida (see the Sweida item below) drew angry reactions from Israeli Druze figures, reported by the Jerusalem Post at 15:51; and Israel is worried about new attacks on the Druze in Sweida (Walla, 06:07). The same interchange was blocked by Druze protesters on 15 July 2025, over the fighting in Sweida (Ynet, Times of Israel). Place: Elyakim, a moshav in the Menashe Heights; the interchange itself is next to it. Approximate map point for Elyakim: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=32.63250,35.06639 (the moshav's coordinates; the exact protest spot is not mapped).

sources.name: Jerusalem Post: reaction to Barrack's remarks, 25 Oct

items.headline: Sweida (Syria): Israel warns Damascus against new attacks on the Druze; Syria reportedly adds troops; the Sweida-Damascus road is blocked
items.lead: Sweida is the Druze-majority province of southern Syria. This week: an Israeli warning, a reported Syrian troop buildup, disputed claims about an Israeli base, a road blockade and an open quarrel between US envoy Tom Barrack and Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri.
items.text: Israel (Walla and the Jerusalem Post, 25 Oct): a security source says Israel fears operatives of the Syrian government, including Bedouin groups coordinated with Syrian security, plan to renew attacks on the Druze in Sweida province. The Israeli Air Force has increased its activity and sent Damascus a warning. The source says Syrian government media accuse Israel of giving weapons, ammunition, money and intelligence to the Druze "National Guard", some of it by air drop. Damascus told Israel it is asserting sovereignty, not targeting civilians (one anonymous Israeli source; unconfirmed). Troops and base (The National, 22 Oct, anonymous security sources): Syria has about 3,000 troops on Sweida's western front, about 1,000 of them sent in the last two weeks, and Israel is reportedly flying in radar and surveillance equipment, possibly for a base; the National Guard has reportedly cordoned off 10 hills; Barrack met President Ahmad al-Sharaa in Damascus on 21 October. A Druze source who opposes al-Hijri told Asharq Al-Awsat (via Arab News, 22 Oct) that the base and offensive reports are "media rumors with no basis"; a National Guard spokesman said Damascus is the one preparing an attack. The reports conflict and I could not confirm either side. Road blockade (Xinhua and Asharq Al-Awsat, 24-25 Oct): Syria's Sweida Media Department says "outlaw groups" closed the Sweida-Damascus highway both ways at the Um al-Zaytoun checkpoint; Enab Baladi says relatives of detainees and missing persons gathered there to demand their release. Barrack (Middle East Eye, Jerusalem Post, Syria Now, 24-25 Oct): in an interview with Mario Nawfal he accused "a particular Druze sheikh" of using perceived Israeli and US backing to persecute other Druze, and called Sweida-Daraa "the captagon manufacturing operation of the world." He did not name the sheikh; media read it as al-Hijri. Al-Hijri's office rejected this as false. Link to Lebanon (single source): the head of Lebanon's Druze religious community, Sheikh Nasr al-Din al-Gharib, told a Sweida media center on 19 October that Sweida's people should decide their own future and that Walid Jumblatt should have waited for an Arab condemnation before his two initiatives (Levant News, 22 Oct).

sources.name: Jerusalem Post, 25 Oct: Israel warns Syria

items.headline: Israeli Druze politics before Tuesday's election: leader Tarif praises Netanyahu on Syria, then says he takes no political side; grievances over the Nation-State Law and building rules continue
items.lead: Sheikh Muwaffaq Tarif, spiritual leader of Israel's Druze, praised Netanyahu on 16 October for stopping the July 2025 killings in Sweida, then said on 17 October that this was not an endorsement.
items.text: On 15 October Netanyahu told a Likud gathering with Druze in Yarka that he spoke to al-Sharaa during the July 2025 fighting: "a very short, very sharp conversation, and the massacre stopped" (i24NEWS, citing his remarks; the Syrian government did not confirm or deny the call). On 16 October Tarif posted a video crediting Netanyahu's decisions, including the strike on Syria's Defense Ministry, with stopping the killings (i24NEWS, News1). On 17 October Tarif issued a statement that he takes no political position and does not call for a vote for any party; he said the community's own concerns are civil, mainly planning and construction and the Kaminitz Law on illegal building, and that some media distorted his words (Panet, JFeed). Background on grievances (older reporting, not new this week): Druze leaders and former officers say the community's service is not matched by equal rights. The 2018 Nation-State Law has been a main complaint, because it has no explicit guarantee of equality, and Tarif asked in November 2023 for constitutional recognition of the community's rights (Jerusalem Post, 25 Oct). In May former IDF Druze Battalion commander Col. (res.) Wajdi Sarhan launched Brit Achim (Brothers' Alliance), the first independent Druze party in decades, aiming for two Knesset seats; there are only three Druze Knesset members now (Times of Israel, 5 May; I did not check whether the party is on the ballot). Druze men are generally drafted, unlike most Israeli Arabs (Jerusalem Post, 25 Oct). I found no new report this week on a Druze-specific draft or reservist dispute or on a new law on Druze status. Druze in Sweida also marched on 7 October with Israeli flags and pictures of Netanyahu and Tarif (Behadrei Haredim, 7 Oct).

Jerusalem Post, 25 Oct: who is drafted

items.headline: Golan Druze turn toward Israel: about 45 percent now hold Israeli citizenship, and some will vote on Tuesday for the first time
items.lead: AFP reports a sharp shift among the roughly 26,000 Druze of the Golan Heights since Israel's 2025 intervention in Sweida.
items.text: AFP (21 Oct, via France 24 and Arab News): about 45 percent of Golan Druze now hold Israeli citizenship, against 2 percent 40 years ago, according to the Interior Ministry. In Majdal Shams there were 3,750 citizenship applications in 2025, against 570 the year before. Wael Mugrabi, mayor of Ein Qiniye, will be the first Golan candidate in a Knesset election. Some residents still boycott Israel, and one young man said he feared being drafted if he took citizenship. The Yeshiva World (22 Oct, single local report) says the mayor of Buq'ata expects 300 to 500 residents to vote on 27 October, against fewer than 75 in 2022, and that some support Likud out of gratitude. Percentages and counts are the Interior Ministry's as relayed by AFP; I did not check them against the ministry.

items.headline: Lula wins a fourth term in the runoff, about 51.7 to 48.3 percent; Flávio Bolsonaro says it is "impossible to concede" and will ask the courts to annul the vote
items.lead: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's runoff, 25 October, with the most votes any Brazilian candidate has ever received.
items.text: With 97 percent of the votes counted, g1 had Lula at 51.74 percent and Flávio at 48.26. Lula received 64,220,485 votes, the most any candidate has ever won in Brazil, and his margin was about 4.38 million votes (g1). Abstention fell to 19.21 percent, from 21.08 percent in the first round (Guardian live blog). Voting was extended to 7 p.m. after Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin acted on complaints that the free buses promised to carry voters were missing in nine states (Guardian live blog; g1). Flávio called the result "sacanagem" (a rude word for a dirty trick), said it was "impossible to concede" and said he would ask the courts to annul the vote; the head of the electoral court (TSE), Justice Nunes Marques, said he had "absolute security" in the result, and Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet also backed the process (g1; Guardian). In his victory speech Lula spoke of "interference" by the big technology companies. The leaders of Mexico (Sheinbaum), Paraguay (Peña), Uruguay (Orsi), Bolivia (Paz), Cuba (Díaz-Canel) and Panama (Mulino) sent congratulations (Guardian live blog). The new term begins on 5 January 2027 (g1).

items.headline: Channel 12: IDF chief Zamir resisted a Netanyahu order for an unspecified military action that could start a clash with Iran before Tuesday; Netanyahu calls the report "nonsense"
items.lead: Channel 12 reported on Sunday night, citing unnamed sources, an "unprecedented confrontation" in which Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir asked for more discussion and for signed documents on the legal authority for the action.
items.text: No details of the action were given, and the report was broadcast under military censorship. A military source told Channel 12 it "could lead to a flare-up with Iran, at a sensitive and dramatic moment", and that army leaders fear an effort "to utilize the Iranian issue for political benefit" (Times of Israel, citing Channel 12). Netanyahu told Channel 14 there was "no fight" with Zamir and that the report was "nonsense" (Times of Israel). i24NEWS and Haaretz report the same fear among senior officers. Opposition leaders backed Zamir: Eisenkot wrote "Netanyahu, I'm watching you"; Lapid said Netanyahu wants a conflict with Iran "just to postpone the election"; Lieberman called it "tantamount to treason" (Times of Israel). Earlier on Sunday, at the Palmahim air base, Netanyahu warned Iran "Don't test us" and said there were intelligence signs that Iran and its allies might attack to disrupt the vote. Trump said there would be no US strike on Iran on Sunday (Ynet); Axios reporter Barak Ravid says the White House was alarmed by Netanyahu's nuclear-blast image (next item) and that Trump's remark may have been meant to calm Tehran (Times of Israel). All of this rests on unnamed sources and cannot be checked.

items.headline: Final weekend: Netanyahu posts an AI image of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv and warns of a "second Holocaust"; Trump repeats his endorsement; Eisenkot says Netanyahu "will stop at nothing"
items.lead: On Sunday Netanyahu posted an AI-made image of a nuclear bomb exploding over Tel Aviv, with text suggesting Israel could face a second Holocaust if he is not re-elected; Eisenkot called it "hysterical".
items.text: Trump reposted his endorsement of Netanyahu overnight: "Vote for him, we need to finish the job we started!" (Ynet; the Times of Israel says this followed a reported request from Netanyahu). At his final Tel Aviv rally Eisenkot (Yashar) said, "I see the polls, I know the data, and I know Netanyahu. He'll stop at nothing, no lie, no extreme measure, to stay in power." He told Likud voters "it is Likud that has strayed from its path" and said Netanyahu "wants a tie", so Yashar must win clearly more seats than Likud (Times of Israel). Also on Sunday: Rabbi Eli Sadan, mentor of Ofer Winter, refused Netanyahu's request to push Winter out of the race and said he hopes Winter's People of Israel party passes the 3.25 percent threshold; United Torah Judaism held a rally of tens of thousands near Bnei Brak against the draft; and the elections committee chairman allowed a meeting of Netanyahu, Ben Gvir and the police chief over the attorney general's objection (Times of Israel). The Central Elections Committee says 7.3 million Israelis can vote at 18,000 ballot boxes on Tuesday 27 October.

sources.name: Times of Israel: Eisenkot's rally and Sadan

items.lead: Read at 4:30 a.m. Israel time on Monday 26 October, about 53.6 million dollars traded on the prime minister market.
items.text: Prime Minister of Israel after the next election: Eisenkot 50.4 percent (down 1.35 points in a day), Netanyahu 25.5 (down 3), Bennett 12.5, Lieberman 2.5. Israeli Legislative Election Winner (most seats; about 3.1 million dollars traded): Yashar 69.5 percent, Likud 30.5. On Sunday the figures were Eisenkot 51.8 and Netanyahu 27.5, and Yashar 71.5.
